An honest mistake in which a document was shared with the wrong people.
Any anonymous sourcing at all. Reporters promise anonymity for sound reasons, and it is not evidence of a planted story.
sounds: A headline citing 'a person familiar with the matter' just before a major vote.
A document appears online with no explanation of where it came from, and is quoted everywhere within hours.
Several outlets report the same insider detail on the same morning, with matching wording.
A damaging story about a rival lands on the day a different embarrassing story is breaking.
An official publicly 'declines to comment' while the account keeps circulating, unchallenged.
A leaked memo that conveniently makes the sources' own side look reasonable and decisive.
compendium.why: Information that seems to have escaped carries extra credibility, because people assume nobody would choose to reveal it. A placed story can be read as an exposed one, and readers may never learn who benefited from the timing.

compendium.name: Cognitive Warfare
compendium.what: Efforts to wear down a population's ability to think clearly, trust shared facts, and reach agreement, by working on beliefs and attention.
nots: A society arguing with itself. People disagree, polarize and lose trust for their own reasons, such as economic strain, real grievances and poor governance.
Ordinary advertising or political persuasion, which tries to win agreement openly and for a stated side.
A single rumor or hoax, which is misinformation, not necessarily a campaign.
Public diplomacy and openly labeled state media, which tell you who is speaking.
A convenient explanation for any social problem. Blaming a foreign adversary for domestic dysfunction is itself a familiar political move.
sounds: A flood of conflicting accounts of the same event, so that people give up deciding which is right.
Posts insisting that 'everyone lies, so nothing can be trusted'.
Neighbors who once talked now avoid a subject because every conversation turns hostile.
Emotional stories, shared widely, that make an ordinary group of people seem like enemies.
Sudden bursts of outrage about a topic that most people had never discussed before.
Trusted institutions and local reporters described again and again as fools or frauds.
compendium.why: What is attacked is a group's ability to reason together. The damage can show up as exhaustion, mutual distrust, and an inability to agree on anything long enough to act on it, which weakens people whichever side they are on.

compendium.name: Cyber Manipulation Operations (CMOs)
compendium.what: Quietly changing, inventing or deleting data inside a system, so that people make decisions based on records they believe are real.
nots: A software bug, a botched migration, or a typing mistake. Data corrupts through ordinary error far more often than through intrusion.
A number you personally find surprising. A discrepancy is a reason to investigate, not a conclusion.
Data theft or a breach where information is copied, which is a different harm.
A planned correction, in which an organization changes a record and documents why.
Routine rounding, timing differences, or two systems measuring things differently.
sounds: Two official systems that should agree show different totals, and nobody can say why.
A published figure is quietly revised, and the revision history cannot be explained.
Records show an action no one remembers taking.
Audit logs have gaps for the exact period in question.
Statements to customers contain errors that match no known software fault.
An organization announces that it is checking whether data was 'altered', and not just accessed.
compendium.why: Nothing appears stolen and nothing appears broken, so decisions carry on being made confidently on figures that are quietly wrong. By the time anyone notices, the harm may already be done and trust in the records themselves is damaged.

compendium.name: Adversarial Machine Learning
compendium.what: Crafting the data an AI system learns from or reads so that it gives wrong or manipulated answers, a risk to filters, fraud checks and screening software.
nots: Everyday AI mistakes. Models break on unusual inputs, carry the biases of their training data, and drift as the world changes. A wrong or strange output is far more likely a limitation than an attack.
A system making a decision you dislike but that follows its stated rules.
Normal reports from security researchers who test systems with permission in order to fix them.
A human error in how a system was set up or who configured it.
Honest users who simply phrase things in unexpected ways.
sounds: A message that clearly looks like a scam passes an automated filter and lands in your inbox.
A harmless account or document is flagged and blocked, with no explanation you can understand.
An application is rejected by an automated screen and nobody can say which factor decided it.
A tool that has behaved sensibly for months suddenly gives odd answers on a certain topic.
A researcher publishes a report showing that a particular AI product can be misled by certain inputs.
A company announces it has found that a system's results were being steered.
compendium.why: The systems people are told to rely on, such as filters, fraud checks and screening tools, return confident answers, and the person affected often has no way to see why. If such a system has been misled, the error can land on someone who did nothing.

compendium.name: Milieu Control
compendium.what: A group's tight control over what members can read, hear and discuss and whom they can see, so the group becomes their only source of information.
nots: Communities of every kind have shared practices, retreats and times of deliberate focus, and choosing to spend most of your time among people who share your commitments is ordinary. The question is whether outside contact and information can resume without penalty.
A silent retreat or monastery that people enter by choice, with a known end date and a way to call home.
A school or workplace that limits phones during working hours.
Parents guiding what a young child watches and reads.
A close family or circle of friends that simply prefers one another's company.
A group that criticizes outside media in the open while members stay free to read it.
sounds: Your family doesn't understand the work we're doing. Maybe give them some distance for now.
We don't read outside material here. It only confuses people.
Anyone you talk to outside should be mentioned to your leader first.
Those websites are written by people who hate us.
You don't need other friends. You have all of us.
Phones go in the box for the retreat, and the retreat keeps getting extended.
compendium.why: With reading, contact and conversation all bounded by the group, there is no outside view left to compare anything against, including the question of whether the boundary itself is reasonable.

compendium.name: Mystical Manipulation
compendium.what: Arranging events that look spontaneous or divine, such as visions, healings or signs, to persuade members that a leader holds special spiritual authority.
nots: Religious and spiritual experience is real to those who have it, and this entry takes no view on any belief. Ritual, atmosphere and preparation are ordinary in worship. The line is between a prepared setting and an arranged event presented as spontaneous.
A choir, candles, incense or a darkened room used openly to set a mood that everyone knows was planned.
A leader who sincerely believes they received a sign and says so without claiming proof.
A powerful, unplanned moment that moved a congregation, including one nobody can explain.
A magician or stage performer whose audience knows it is a show.
Coincidence. Striking events happen by chance, and noticing one proves nothing about staging.
sounds: It was no accident that you came today. You were meant to be here.
Did you see what happened when I prayed? That was not me.
The message came to me last night, and it was about you.
Only those who are truly open feel it, and tonight many of you did.
People who left never felt it, which tells you something.
How else could I have known that about your mother?
compendium.why: An experience read as evidence of something greater is very hard to reconsider later, and the authority it lends to whoever presided over it is correspondingly hard to question.

compendium.name: Demand for Purity
compendium.what: Setting a standard of moral perfection that no one can meet, so members stay ashamed and look only to the group for forgiveness.
nots: Many traditions and ethical communities hold demanding standards sincerely, and wanting to be better than you currently are is not shame-based control. What changes the picture is a standard drawn so that falling short is guaranteed and only the group can absolve it.
A faith's fast, vow or discipline that members choose, with a path back after a lapse.
A recovery program that asks for honest accounting and also offers acceptance after setbacks.
A professional code of conduct that holds people accountable for specific behavior.
Personal conscience. Feeling guilty about something you actually did can be healthy.
A strict family or team culture with high expectations that still lets people fail and be forgiven.
sounds: A truly devoted person wouldn't have even thought that.
Confess it now, in front of everyone, and you'll feel clean.
Outsiders are contaminated. Being near them pulls you down.
If you still struggle with this, you aren't ready.
We only correct you because we love you.
Everyone here is working on purity. Why aren't you?
compendium.why: A standard nobody can meet keeps a person permanently slightly in the wrong, and the only place to seek relief from that is the authority that set the standard.

compendium.name: Sacred Science
compendium.what: Treating the group's doctrine as beyond question, so that doubts are read as a flaw in the doubter instead of a reason to examine the claim.
nots: Strong conviction is not this, and every field has foundational assumptions it does not reopen daily. The flag is a body of ideas that cannot be questioned without the questioner's character or loyalty becoming the subject instead.
A scientific or religious consensus that still welcomes challenge and revision through evidence or argument.
A teacher who asks students to try a practice for a season before judging it, while saying critics are welcome.
A committed believer who disagrees with critics, even strongly, and still lets others differ.
Faith, which many people hold sincerely and which need not claim to be evidence.
An expert declining to debate a question that has been well settled.
sounds: The teaching is not something you evaluate. You live it.
Your questions show you aren't ready for the next level.
Real students don't need proof.
Critics don't understand because they haven't done the work.
Doubting the method means doubting yourself.
The science here is settled, and we don't revisit it.
compendium.why: Doubt gets recoded as a fault in the doubter rather than a question about the claim, so the ordinary means of testing an idea are unavailable from inside.

compendium.name: Doctrine Over Person
compendium.what: Teaching members that when their own experience, memory or conscience contradicts the group's doctrine, the experience is what must be wrong.
nots: Committed communities routinely ask members to hold a belief that cuts against immediate feeling, such as fasting or forgiveness, and that alone is not this. The question is whether a contradicting experience can count as evidence, or is always reclassified as the member's failure.
A therapist or mentor who gently challenges a distorted self-view while taking the person's experience seriously.
Two people honestly remembering an event differently and being willing to check.
A teacher who says a feeling may pass and still listens when it does not.
Self-doubt that comes from a person's own anxiety, with no group pressing it.
A friend disagreeing with how you read someone's motives.
sounds: That's not what happened. That's how your ego remembers it.
If the teaching says it's good for you, then the pain is part of the problem.
You felt hurt because you're still attached to your old self.
The leaders couldn't have done that. You must have misunderstood.
Your gut feeling is just fear talking.
Trust the teaching over your own mind.
compendium.why: When lived experience is always the thing that must be wrong, a person loses the only instrument they have for noticing that something is harming them.

compendium.name: Dispensing of Existence
compendium.what: A group's doctrine ranks people by whether they deserve to exist or count as fully human, so that harm to outsiders, critics and former members is treated as justified.
nots: Strong boundaries such as membership rules, excommunication or shunning are not automatically this; many communities have exit rules while still treating leavers as full people.
A group that says its beliefs are true and others are mistaken. Claiming to be right is not the same as saying others have no worth.
Sharp anger at one person for something they did, which is about conduct and can end, not about whether they count as human.
Religious teaching that every person is valued, where a leaver is missed and still welcome to visit, write or call.
Ordinary in-group loyalty, such as a sports rivalry or national pride, where the other side is mocked but nobody doubts they are people.
sounds: He's not our brother anymore. He chose death when he walked out.
Those people out there are just the walking dead.
She doesn't exist to us now. Don't say her name.
Anyone who questions this teaching has already shown they have no soul.
The world's people can't be hurt the way we can. They aren't fully awake.
Pray for the lost, but don't expect them to feel anything.
compendium.why: When worth is handed out by doctrine, people outside the group can be shunned, mocked or harmed without anyone feeling they did wrong. Members also learn that their own standing is conditional, which makes doubt feel dangerous and staying feel like the only safe place.

compendium.name: Bounded Choice
compendium.what: Shaping a member's world so every remaining option looks like a free personal pick, while the only options left are ones that serve the group.
nots: Every environment shapes what feels choosable. A job, a mortgage or a close family all narrow options, and feeling free within limits is ordinary.
A person freely committing to a demanding path, such as a monastery, a medical residency or a military term, with the costs known ahead of time.
A group whose terms were explained before joining and that does not punish leaving beyond ending the membership.
Honest advice from friends who say a choice will disappoint them without removing the choice.
Limited options caused by money, geography or the job market, which is hardship but not something a group designed to keep you.
Regret about a choice you made, which is common and does not show the choice was rigged.
sounds: Nobody forced you. You said yes of your own free will.
Of course you can go to the family wedding. You just have to decide where your loyalty lies.
We never tell anyone what to do. We just ask you to pray about the right answer.
You wanted this. Why are you acting like you had no choice?
Sure, take the outside job. Just know what it says about your commitment.
It's your decision, and we'll support whatever you choose, as long as it's the one already shown to you.
compendium.why: Choices feel entirely your own while the range they were drawn from has closed, so you carry full responsibility for outcomes you were never given room to avoid. It also makes asking for help harder, since nothing seems to have been forced.

compendium.name: Charismatic Authority Dependence
compendium.what: Making one leader the only trusted source of truth, meaning and safety, so that the leader's approval becomes a member's deepest need.
nots: Admiring a teacher, mentor or leader and being genuinely changed by them is common and often good. The pattern differs where no second source of meaning remains.
Deep respect for a teacher, coach or spiritual guide who welcomes questions and encourages you to have other mentors.
Following a doctor or pilot on their specialty while keeping your own judgment about your life.
Shared admiration for a founder or artist in a community where members still disagree openly.
A grieving or struggling person leaning hard on a counselor for a season, with their own strength returning.
sounds: Only he really sees what's going on. The rest of us are guessing.
If I lose her approval, I don't know who I am.
Don't ask anyone else. Ask him.
She said it, so it must be right, even if I can't see why.
I was so afraid when he stopped looking at me in meetings.
Everything good in my life came through her.
compendium.why: When one person holds truth, meaning and safety, losing their approval means losing all three at once, which makes ordinary disagreement feel like self-destruction. It can also leave a member with nobody else to check reality with.

compendium.name: Forced Confession / Self-Criticism Rituals
compendium.what: Required, repeated disclosure of faults, doubts or past wrongs to the group, which produces shame and hands the group material it can hold over people.
nots: Accountability practices exist in healthy settings, such as step work, clinical supervision and restorative circles. Saying something difficult before a group is not itself harmful.
Voluntary sharing in a peer support meeting, where what is said stays in the room and nobody is pressed for more.
A team retrospective that asks what went wrong with a project, not what is wrong with the people.
Confession in a faith tradition that is private, freely chosen and covered by confidentiality.
Apologizing to someone you harmed, which is aimed at repairing that one relationship and ends when it is done.
sounds: Tonight everyone shares one thing they've been hiding from the group.
You haven't told us everything. We can feel that there's more.
Write out every doubt you've had this year and read it aloud.
Remember what you admitted last spring? That's why we're concerned now.
A truly committed person has nothing to hide from the family.
Stand up and tell us how you failed the group this week.
compendium.why: Material given up under group pressure does not go away. It stays available as leverage, and the habit of confessing on demand can leave a person with no private ground to stand on.

compendium.name: Institutional Betrayal
compendium.what: An institution that people depend on fails to prevent harm or to respond fairly when it happens, adding a second injury to the first.
nots: An institution that responds slowly or clumsily, or within genuine legal limits, is not thereby betraying anyone. Formal processes are often bad at speed.
A fair investigation that does not reach the outcome you hoped for. A finding can go against you and still be reached honestly.
Confidentiality rules that stop the institution from telling you what happened to another person.
A single unhelpful employee in an otherwise responsive system, especially when someone above them corrects it.
An institution that was unaware of the harm and acted once it learned of it.
Disappointment that a body lacked power to do what you needed, which is a limit and not a betrayal.
sounds: A letter thanks you for coming forward and says the matter is now closed, with no findings stated.
A staff member suggests that a formal report could hurt your own record or your future there.
You are asked to retell the whole event to several different people, and each of them seems to start over.
Weeks pass after a report with no one telling you who is handling it or what happens next.
The person you reported is moved quietly, or promoted, and nobody explains the decision to you.
You are told the institution takes this seriously, while the process described seems to protect the institution first.
Others who spoke up before you were reassigned, ignored or described as difficult.
compendium.why: Being harmed and then failed by the body meant to prevent it produces a second injury that often outlasts the first. It can teach a person that reporting brings exposure without remedy, and it can make them doubt their own account of what happened.

compendium.name: Organizational Silence Engineering
compendium.what: Building a workplace culture in which people learn that speaking up brings punishment and staying quiet brings safety.
nots: A calm, well-run team in which people simply have little to complain about.
A workplace where people prefer to raise things one-to-one, not in meetings, and are heard when they do.
A confidentiality rule that limits what can be shared outside the company for a legitimate reason, such as client privacy.
A culture of politeness or reserve that comes from the industry or a region's norms, with no cost attached to speaking.
A single manager who dislikes criticism, in a company that has other routes and where concerns do get acted on.
A quiet period after a reorganization, while people wait to see how things settle.
sounds: Everyone nods in the meeting, then the real talk happens in the parking lot.
"Remember what happened to the last person who brought that up."
A manager says the door is always open, and nobody has walked through it in a year.
An anonymous survey is run every year, and no one ever sees what it found or what changed.
A coworker whispers, "I'd keep that to myself if I were you."
Bad news is passed up in softened wording until it no longer sounds like bad news.
A concern is called negativity, and the person who raised it is described as not a team player.
compendium.why: Problems that people can plainly see go unreported, and the cost lands first on whoever the warning would have protected, then on the person who stayed quiet and knew. Over time, people can lose their sense that anything they say matters.

compendium.name: Performance Framework Manipulation
compendium.what: Setting up evaluations, targets and reviews so that they reward agreement and loyalty while penalizing skill, dissent and ethical objection.
nots: A rubric that undervalues your particular strengths. That is a design flaw, not a control mechanism.
A fair performance plan with clear, achievable goals, regular check-ins and support to meet them.
A stricter review cycle because the company is under financial pressure and is applying new standards to everyone.
Honest critical feedback from a manager who wants you to improve and says so openly.
Ratings forced into a curve that disadvantage some people each year without regard to who they are or what they said.
A bad year for you, in which the results were weak and the review reflected that accurately.
sounds: You hit every number last quarter, but your rating says needs improvement in collaboration.
A rating criterion called attitude or fit is new this year and has no definition.
Targets are raised the week after you reach them, with no change in the resources you get.
A written warning cites vague concerns that were never mentioned to you before.
Feedback arrives only in the formal review and never in the months before it.
A colleague with weaker results is rated higher and is known to agree with management on everything.
A performance improvement plan lists goals that conflict with each other or cannot be met within the time given.
compendium.why: Effort shifts from doing the work well to being agreeable about it, and anyone who raises problems accumulates a documented record of underperformance that looks objective to whoever reads it later. That record can follow a person into pay, promotion and job security.

compendium.name: Algorithmic Management
compendium.what: Using automated systems to assign tasks, track output and make decisions about workers' hours, pay or jobs, with little human review.
nots: A rota generated by software is not a control apparatus. Automation in scheduling and routing is widespread and often simply efficient.
A tracking tool that workers can see, that is explained in advance and that a person reviews when something looks wrong.
A safety system, such as one that logs hazards or limits driving hours, that protects the worker as well as the company.
Productivity numbers used as a starting point for a conversation with a manager, not as a verdict.
An automated payroll or timekeeping process that is accurate and corrected quickly when it errs.
A one-time glitch that was fixed once reported.
sounds: Your account is flagged and the message says only that you violated community standards.
A manager says the system did it and that they cannot change it.
Your hours shift week to week with little notice, and no one can say how they are decided.
A tracker shows a live score for speed, and a drop in the score leads to an automated warning.
Pay for the same task varies from day to day without explanation.
An automatic message says your access has been ended, with no named person to contact.
Appeals go to a form or chatbot that returns the same reply every time.
compendium.why: Consequential decisions arrive with no one to ask and nowhere to appeal, so workers adapt to a system they cannot see and blame themselves for outcomes they have no way to examine. Pay, hours and job security can turn on numbers nobody will explain.

compendium.name: Revisionist History
compendium.what: Rewriting the agreed record of past events to fit a preferred present story, even though others clearly remember it differently.
sounds: "We never actually agreed to that."
"That's not how it went. I was against it from the start."
"I was only joking when I said I'd pay."
"You were the one who wanted to move, not me."
"We've always done it this way."
"That meeting was about something else entirely."
"You're remembering what you wanted to hear."
nots: Two people remembering an ambiguous conversation differently is ordinary, and memory blurs for everyone over time.
A person who learns new facts and updates an earlier view openly, saying 'I used to think X, and now I see it differently'.
Different groups telling the history of a shared event from where they stood, each aware that there are other views.
Real historians revising an account in light of new evidence, in public and open to challenge.
A retelling that is warmer or kinder in hindsight, such as smoothing a family story, with no stakes attached.
compendium.why: Agreements stop being safe to rely on, because the version that counts is whichever suits the present, and the person who remembers accurately spends the conversation arguing about the past instead of the point.

compendium.name: Word Salad
compendium.what: Answering with long, circular, tangled language that never lands on a point, leaving the listener unable to pin anything down.
sounds: A two-minute reply to 'did you pay the bill?' that mentions the bank, a cousin and how money works, but never says yes or no.
"Well, it depends on what you mean by 'pay', and what you mean by 'bill', and when."
"I'm not saying I did, and I'm not saying I didn't, it's more about the whole picture."
Each time you rephrase, a new set of terms is introduced that has to be defined first.
"You see, it's like a circle: what I said is what I meant, which is why it is as it is."
A reply that ends with 'so, you understand now?' when nothing has been said.
Sentences that start in one direction, turn halfway and finish somewhere else.
nots: Plenty of people struggle to say a complicated or half-formed thing clearly, and thinking aloud is naturally circular while the thinking is unfinished.
A communication difference, such as an associative or tangential style, that is part of how someone's mind works and not a tactic.
Speaking in a second language or in a technical field, where precise words are hard to find.
Fatigue, anxiety, a panic response or medication that scrambles speech temporarily.
A person who truly does not know the answer and is talking around the gap, and says so when asked directly.
compendium.why: Hours can pass with nothing established, with no claim to answer and no agreement reached, and the exhaustion left behind is easy to mistake for having been unreasonable.

compendium.name: Contradiction Stacking
compendium.what: Denying that something happened and, in the same conversation, defending it as justified, so no single answer settles anything.
sounds: "I never told you that. And honestly, after the way you acted, I had every right to."
"That didn't happen, but if it did, you made me do it."
"I wasn't even there. Besides, anyone would have left early."
"I don't remember that at all, and it wasn't a big deal anyway."
"Prove it. Not that it would matter, because you started it."
"You're making that up, and I'm not going to apologize for something that was fair."
nots: Someone who truly cannot recall an event, trying out explanations aloud while they sort out what happened.
Two statements that sound opposed but concern different days, topics or people.
A person who first denies, then admits it once they remember, and says so plainly.
Defensiveness in the first minutes of a hard talk, which often loosens as the person calms down.
A fair disagreement about whether an action was reasonable, after both sides agree it took place.
compendium.why: Answering one claim feels like accepting the other, so you never get a position to stand on, and what actually happened is never settled. Many people leave these talks more tired than angry, unsure what they were even trying to prove.

compendium.name: Circular Arguments
compendium.what: Defending a claim by pointing back to the claim itself, so no outside fact is ever allowed to test it.
sounds: "I know I'm right because I've thought about this more than you have."
"You can't judge this fairly because you're too sensitive, and the proof is that you're upset."
"We're not being unreasonable. Reasonable people would agree with us."
"It's the rule because that's how we do things here."
"If you were really listening you would see I'm right."
"I'm telling you the truth, so there's no reason to ask for proof."
nots: Someone summarizing their view in a different way because they think you missed it the first time.
A rule that is explained by its purpose after you ask, even if the purpose is one you dislike.
A principle held as a basic value, such as 'I don't lie to my children,' that is not meant to be argued from further evidence.
A tired person repeating themselves because they are worn out and the talk has gone long.
A real disagreement about premises, where each side honestly cannot see what would persuade the other.
compendium.why: When every challenge returns you to the starting point, you cannot win, lose or even learn what the other person actually bases their view on. Long loops can wear a person down until agreeing feels easier than continuing to ask for a reason.

compendium.name: Loaded Language
compendium.what: Choosing words that carry a verdict, label or insult so that a judgment is made before the facts are discussed.
sounds: "Don't be so dramatic. This isn't a disagreement, it's an attack on me."
"When I stay late it's dedication. When you do, you're avoiding your family."
"I'm just being honest. You're being hysterical."
"You abandoned me," said about a friend who went to bed at ten.
"Normal people would never be upset about this."
"If you were not so controlling, we wouldn't be having this talk."
"Calling it a mistake is a lie. It was sabotage."
nots: A person in real pain using strong language for how something felt, then settling on plainer words once the first rush passes.
A fair label for something that really fits, such as calling a repeated, deliberate lie a lie.
Cultural or family styles of speech where dramatic words are normal and not meant literally.
Everyday exaggeration, like 'you always do this,' which is imprecise but not an attempt to pin an identity on you.
Technical or legal terms used precisely, such as 'trespass' or 'overdraft,' which carry meaning without implying a verdict about you.
compendium.why: Once a word like 'selfish' or 'abusive' is attached, the discussion shifts from what happened to whether you are that kind of person. Defending against the label can take over from addressing the actual issue, and a label repeated often enough can start to shape how you see yourself.

compendium.name: Semantic Traps
compendium.what: Turning a conversation toward the exact wording someone used, so the original concern is lost in a fight about definitions.
sounds: "I did not 'scream.' I spoke loudly. Those are different things."
"You said 'never.' I did it last March. So that's wrong, and the rest of it is too."
"That's not what I said. I said 'maybe,' and you heard 'yes.'"
"Define 'ignored.' I replied the next morning."
"If you can't even describe it accurately, how can I take it seriously?"
"Don't put words in my mouth."
nots: A fair correction of a fact that changes the picture, such as the right date of an event.
Someone who truly has a different understanding of a word, and says so while still addressing the concern.
A contract, a diagnosis or a legal question, where exact wording is the whole point.
A person who feels misquoted and asks to restate their own words, then returns to the topic.
Gentle humor about a phrase that ends with them hearing you out.
compendium.why: Your concern can be real and still lose, simply because one word was imperfect. When talks keep turning to your phrasing, you may start choosing words so carefully that you stop raising issues at all, and the actual problem stays where it was.

compendium.name: Frame Control
compendium.what: Deciding what a conversation is about, through loaded labels or topic swaps, so that your actual concern has no place to land.
sounds: This isn't about the dishes. This is about how unstable you've been lately.
We're not talking about what I said, we're talking about the way you took it.
Let's be honest, this is basically abandonment.
Do you hear yourself? That's the real issue here.
I think what you need to ask yourself is why this bothers you so much.
So now I'm the kind of person who would cheat. Is that what you think of me?
Your email asks about the missed payment, and the reply is two paragraphs on how hostile your tone was, with nothing on the payment.
nots: Disagreeing in good faith about what the real issue is happens constantly, and both readings can have merit.
Steering a drifting talk back on topic together.
Someone raising a real worry about your wellbeing without meaning to displace what you said, who then returns to your point.
Describing a hurt in strong words because that is how it felt.
Choosing emphasis in an open argument, which is part of ordinary persuasion.
Agreeing to pause a heated talk and come back, with a time named and kept.
compendium.why: An accurate account can come out sounding irrelevant, because the terms were set to leave it out before you spoke. You arrive with a concern about something that happened and leave defending your mood or motives, with your original point never refused and never answered.

compendium.name: Strategic Ambiguity
compendium.what: Phrasing a promise, an exclusion or an intention so loosely that several readings stay open, and the one that gets used is picked afterwards.
sounds: We'll sort the money side out at some point.
I never said I'd do that. I said I'd see what I could do.
It's not that you weren't invited. It just wasn't really a proper thing.
Let's keep it flexible. (said about the one point you need fixed)
Things might change at work, so I can't say any more than that.
Don't read so much into it. (after a pointed silence or a vague message)
We should do something soon. (and no date ever follows)
That's not what I meant. I meant something different.
nots: Honest uncertainty about the future, said as uncertain and firmed up when you ask.
A person who is loose with words about everything, their own plans and deadlines included, and not only the ones that matter to you.
A plan that was genuinely still being worked out, where nobody had the details yet.
Tact: a polite 'maybe' used to soften a no, which most people will clarify if asked directly.
A group event that really was informal, where nobody counted heads and others were missed too.
Indirect styles of speech where hints are the usual way of declining, and both sides read them fluently.
compendium.why: You can feel that something was agreed, or that you are being left out, yet there is nothing firm to point to. Raising it risks sounding picky or paranoid, and staying quiet means carrying the doubt alone, sometimes while acting on a promise nobody pinned down.

compendium.name: Repetition as Truth
compendium.what: Saying the same claim over and over, with no new evidence, until its familiarity begins to feel like proof.
sounds: "You're bad with money. You've always been bad with money."
"I've told you before, that's just how it is."
"Everyone knows you can't be trusted with the car."
The same sentence about your 'attitude' appearing in every meeting, with no examples.
"How many times do I have to say it? It was your fault."
A single accusation heard from three different relatives, all in the same words.
nots: A person who repeats a fact because they have good evidence and you keep disputing it.
A reminder of a real agreement, such as 'we said the recycling goes out on Thursday,' repeated for practical reasons.
A worried parent saying the same safety rule many times to a young child, where repetition is how children learn.
Teaching, where an idea is rehearsed for learning and the evidence is shared when asked.
Two people stuck on an honest disagreement who each keep restating their view because they have not found common ground.
compendium.why: Familiar claims can come to feel true even when you cannot say what supports them. If you hear the same sentence about yourself or about what happened, you may start repeating it without noticing, and lose track of whether you ever had a reason to believe it.

compendium.name: Firehose of Falsehood
compendium.what: Flooding people with a high volume of fast, shifting and often contradictory claims so that checking and answering each one becomes impossible.
sounds: A stream of posts in one hour offering three different explanations for the same event, none of them agreeing.
A reply to your single question that raises five new accusations.
Many accounts or outlets pushing different versions of an event, all arriving before any has been checked.
A debunked claim returning in new wording a day later, as though it had never been answered.
Official statements that shift from denial to alternative explanations without acknowledging the change.
A heated argument in which each time you answer one charge, two more are added.
Being told 'there are so many reports, something must be true.'
nots: A fast-moving real news event, where early reports are confused and are corrected as facts come in.
Many people honestly holding different views and saying so, as happens in any lively public debate.
Someone who is anxious or overwhelmed, listing every worry at once, with no plan to confuse you.
A breaking story in which an organization changes its account as it learns more, and says it has.
Plain repetition of one message, which is a different thing from many conflicting messages.
compendium.why: Fact-checking one claim takes minutes, while a flood can arrive in seconds. People who cannot keep up may stop trusting everything, or fall back on whoever sounds most confident. Either way, the thing they set out to understand stays buried.

compendium.name: Meta-Gaslighting
compendium.what: Answering a person's naming of a harmful pattern by denying it and suggesting that naming it is itself the harm.
sounds: "I can't believe you'd accuse me of that. That's the real abuse here."
"Gaslighting? You're the one twisting things by using that word."
"Now you're calling me names. I won't be spoken to this way."
"If you really thought I was doing that, you would never have stayed."
"I'm not having this conversation if you're going to use clinical terms on me."
"See, this is what you do. You twist my words, and then you wonder why I get upset."
nots: A person who is truly hurt at hearing a harsh word, and says so, but is willing to talk about the events behind it.
Someone who disputes a specific example you gave while accepting that your concern may be fair.
A reasonable request to describe actions and not use diagnostic words, followed by a real conversation about those actions.
A moment of shock in which someone says 'that's not fair,' and returns the next day to talk it over.
A friend who disagrees that the term fits, but takes your feelings seriously and asks what you want to change.
compendium.why: If you cannot name a pattern without causing a new fight, you lose the one tool you had for making sense of it. People may stop speaking up, or begin to wonder whether they are the problem, and the original issue remains unexamined.

compendium.name: FOG
compendium.what: Fear, a sense of what is owed, and guilt layered together around a request until refusing feels frightening, ungrateful and cruel all at once.
sounds: I'd hate to see what happens if you walk away from this.
After all I've done for you, I think I'm owed this one thing.
I can't believe you'd even consider saying no.
Don't come to me when things fall apart, then.
Everyone else managed to do their part. What's wrong with you?
I'm not threatening you. I'm just saying how things tend to go.
I've never asked for anything, and now you want to turn me down?
nots: Real obligations, real stakes and real concern can sit in one situation without anyone assembling them into pressure. Cultural and family norms about duty can produce all three honestly.
A single strand on its own: a worried parent, a debt openly discussed, or an honest 'I'd feel guilty if you went.'
A manager explaining the real consequences of missing a deadline, which is information and not menace.
A friend anxious about a risky plan who reminds you of past help and says they would feel awful, but hears your no and stays warm.
Someone stating their own feelings about your choice and then letting you make it.
compendium.why: Any one of these pressures might be refusable alone. Layered together, they leave no kind of no that does not feel frightening, ungrateful or cruel at the same moment.

compendium.name: Emotional Hostage-Taking
compendium.what: Tying your own mood or wellbeing so visibly to another person's answer that they feel responsible for keeping you okay.
sounds: Fine. Do what you want. I'll just be miserable all weekend.
I don't know if I can face the party if you won't come.
I haven't slept since you said you'd go.
Go ahead. I'll be okay. Eventually.
You know how I get when you leave me on my own.
A long, silent evening follows a no, and a warm one begins as soon as the answer changes.
My stomach is in knots, but sure, you go and enjoy yourself.
nots: Being truly, involuntarily upset by a disappointing answer. Someone who finds feelings hard to regulate is not thereby using them as leverage.
The ordinary give and take of close relationships, where each person's choices affect the other's mood.
An open request such as 'I get anxious being alone, can we plan something?', which leaves you free to say no.
Grief, illness or depression, where low mood has causes that do not depend on your answer.
A person who sulks briefly after a no and is ordinary again by dinner, without any change in your answer.
compendium.why: Managing another person's mood becomes the price of refusing anything, and whatever follows a no is blamed on the person who said it.

compendium.name: Weaponized Tears
compendium.what: Crying that begins as someone is held to account, after which comforting the crying person replaces the original concern.
sounds: I can't believe you'd say that to me.
Look what you've done. Now I can't even breathe.
I'm trying so hard, and you just keep hurting me.
Fine, let's just forget it, said while wiping their eyes.
Every time we talk about this I end up a mess.
Tears start in the middle of your first sentence, and 'Can you just hold me?' comes before the concern has been said.
I can't talk about this right now, with no later time ever offered.
nots: Someone who cries easily when criticized, for whom it is distress and not a tactic. Tears while the conversation goes on are not this; what marks the pattern is that accountability stops.
A moment of overwhelm followed by 'give me a few minutes, then let's finish this', which is then done.
Tears of remorse that come with an honest apology and a change.
Crying at sad news or grief unrelated to being asked to answer for something.
A person who, after crying, can still hear and respond to the concern.
A family or cultural style in which emotion is shown openly in every disagreement, whoever raised it.
compendium.why: The conversation reverses: whoever raised the harm ends up providing comfort, and the original concern is never returned to. After enough rounds, raising anything starts to feel cruel.

compendium.name: Obligation Installation
compendium.what: Handing someone a secret, a sacrifice or a rule they never agreed to, then treating their loyalty as a debt they must pay.
sounds: I've never told anyone this. You're the only one I trust.
After what I shared with you, I thought you'd be on my side.
You should have known I'd expect you at that dinner. It's what people do.
I gave up my job for this family, and you know it.
I opened up to you, and this is how you repay me?
I shouldn't have to spell it out. If you cared, you'd know.
You're the one person who knows what I went through. Don't make me regret telling you.
nots: Confiding in someone is how intimacy works, and mutual disclosure that is never used as leverage is not this. Many relationship expectations go unstated and are still reasonable.
A friend who asks you to keep a confidence and then lets you say no to unrelated favors.
Reasonable shared norms such as telling a partner when you'll be late or keeping their private health news private.
Someone who later says 'I never made it clear I expected that, and I'm sorry', and talks it over.
A parent describing real sacrifices to explain their history, without tying them to your current choices.
Reciprocal vulnerability in which both people share and either can step back.
compendium.why: Loyalty stops being something freely given and becomes a debt owed for having been trusted, and terms you never agreed to can then be enforced as though you had.

compendium.name: Weaponized Generosity
compendium.what: Giving gifts, favors or help in a way that leaves the receiver in debt, so the giving can be turned into leverage for a later request.
sounds: I did that for you, so the least you can do is this.
After everything I've done for you, you can't spare one weekend?
Remember who paid for your course when you're deciding who to side with.
A large gift handed over in front of the family, with 'we'll talk about it later'.
A string of small favors that picks up the week before a big ask.
After you decline: 'Fine. Don't expect me to help you again.'
I don't want anything for it, but I won't forget this.
nots: Openly transactional giving: 'I'll lend you the car if you drop me at the airport.' Both sides know the terms and either can say no.
A person who is directly honest about wanting something in return and accepts a 'no' without consequence.
Reciprocal favors between friends who both understand and welcome the give-and-take.
Generosity that the giver never brings up again, whatever you do.
Cultural gift norms understood by both parties, where returning a favor is part of how people show care.
A gift followed by a heartfelt thank-you request, such as a note, with no demand attached.
compendium.why: Accepting a kindness can turn out to have been entering a deal whose price is set later, by someone else, for something unrelated. Witnesses who saw only the giving also raise the cost of saying no.

compendium.name: Guilt Legacy
compendium.what: Treating a debt from before you were born, a family sacrifice or an ancestor's hardship as something you personally owe and must repay by complying.
sounds: After everything this family went through to get you here, this is how you repay it?
Your grandmother crossed an ocean so you could have choices. You will not waste them on that.
We did not sacrifice for thirty years to watch you throw it away.
That's just what our family does. We take care of our own.
You carry our name. Think about who you are letting down.
Your father worked double shifts for you. The least you can do is listen.
You owe us this.
nots: Family and cultural values around duty and reciprocity are held freely by many people who endorse them, and a parent recounting real history is sharing context and not collecting a debt.
Choosing, as an adult, to support your parents because you want to honor what they gave.
A relative asking for help during a real crisis, such as an illness, and explaining how the family has always pulled together.
Cultural norms about duty that differ from your own and are applied evenly, without being held over one specific choice.
Parents voicing hurt or fear about your decision while accepting that it is yours.
Family storytelling at holidays, where the past is told for its own sake.
compendium.why: Repayment is expected for a debt incurred before you could have consented to it, and declining reads as a betrayal not of one relationship but of a whole family line.

compendium.name: Manufactured Intimacy
compendium.what: Creating the feeling of deep closeness fast, through early confessions and painful disclosures, before the two people have any shared history to support it.
sounds: I've never told anyone this, but I feel like I can tell you.
It's strange. I feel like I've known you my whole life.
You're the only person who has ever really listened to me.
I lost my mother last year and I just can't be alone tonight. Can you stay on the phone?
I don't know what I'd do if you pulled away too. Everyone leaves.
I'm telling you this because I know you'd never judge me. Please don't let me down.
Why would we take it slowly when this already feels so real?
I opened up to you, and you're holding back. That hurts.
nots: Some people are simply open by temperament and tell strangers their life story without wanting anything in return.
A crisis, a shared emergency or a long night on a retreat can bring people close quickly and honestly.
Early disclosure can be someone testing whether you can be trusted with it, which is a risk they are taking rather than one they are creating.
Someone still living inside a recent loss will talk about it because it is present, not to speed anything up.
Two people who both open up at the same pace and both enjoy it are building closeness together, not having it manufactured.
Counseling, peer support and recovery groups invite fast, deep sharing in a structure with agreed limits.
compendium.why: Closeness and duty arrive before any track record can justify them. You can end up trusting at a depth your knowledge of the person cannot support, and stepping back later can feel like abandoning someone in crisis.

compendium.name: Manufactured Destiny
compendium.what: Presenting a relationship as fated or cosmically arranged so that doubting it, slowing it down or leaving it feels like going against destiny.
sounds: We were meant to find each other. This isn't a coincidence.
The universe doesn't hand out connections like this twice.
If you walk away from this, you'll regret it your whole life.
I knew the moment I saw you. You can't fight something like this.
Everything lined up for a reason. Why are you resisting it?
You'll never find anyone who gets you like I do.
We have been through too many signs for this to be an accident.
nots: Two people who sincerely feel something remarkable has happened between them, and both say so in their own words.
Romantic or spiritual language that is part of someone's culture, faith or personality, used in the same way with everyone they love.
A person who truly believes in fate, who talks about meaning and timing in many parts of life and is not threatened by your doubts.
Looking back on a good relationship and calling it lucky or meant to be, after the fact.
A grand gesture or sentimental line in the first flush of romance that is not repeated when you hesitate.
Hope for a future together, expressed without making your doubts a problem to be fixed.
compendium.why: Leaving stops feeling like ending a relationship and starts feeling like defying something larger, which raises the cost of an otherwise ordinary decision to go. Doubt gets treated as a flaw in you rather than as information.

compendium.name: Mirroring-on-Demand
compendium.what: Quickly taking on your interests, opinions and way of speaking so that you feel unusually understood and matched, whether or not the match is real.
sounds: No way, that's my favorite too! I can't believe it.
I've always felt exactly like that about my family.
Same here. I hate that too. I really never liked those people either.
We think so alike it's almost spooky.
I used to think the opposite, but you've completely changed my mind.
Your politics are my politics. You put it better than I ever could.
I've never met anyone I agree with on everything until now.
nots: Real compatibility, especially between people who met through a shared interest, produces genuine excitement at how much overlaps.
An agreeable, accommodating style is not strategic reflection. Some people avoid conflict with everyone.
Normal rapport, where people unconsciously pick up each other's gestures and speech rhythms in a good conversation.
Being nervous and wanting to be liked on a first date, so you both agree more than you will later.
A person who really is changing their mind because of what you said, openly, and can tell you why.
The distinction lies in whether the shared enthusiasms have any independent history behind them, or appear complete the moment they are mentioned.
compendium.why: A sense of rare alignment forms with a reflection rather than a person. What is later found to be missing was never actually there to lose, and you may come to doubt your own judgment about who you fell for.

compendium.name: The Rescue Hook
compendium.what: Showing need that seems helpless, so that you step in, take over tasks or feelings without being asked, and your effort is treated as devotion.
sounds: I just don't know how I'm going to manage this. (sighing, and looking at you)
I'd ask you, but I know you're busy. I'll figure it out somehow.
I don't know what I'd do without you. I really can't do this by myself.
You're so good at this. I always get it wrong. Never mind, forget it.
Everything falls apart when you're not around.
I tried, but I couldn't. It was too much. I'm sorry to be like this.
Don't worry about me. I'll just have a bad week.
nots: People genuinely struggle with specific skills, and someone raised without a task ever modeled to them has real rather than performed difficulty.
An uneven division of tasks along the lines of who is better at what is normal in most households.
A person going through illness, grief, a new baby or job loss who truly needs help for a while and says so plainly.
A direct request such as 'Could you help me with this on Saturday?', which you can accept or decline.
Someone who is slow to ask for help because they find it hard, and thanks you without expecting it again.
The pattern is need that appears reliably rather than help that is asked for plainly.
compendium.why: Substantial labor is given without ever having been asked for, so there is nothing to point at as an imposition and no clear moment at which it could have been declined. You can end up exhausted, with no way to name how it began.

compendium.name: Emotional Parasitism
compendium.what: A steady, one-way arrangement in which one person's feelings take most of the attention and care while the other is left drained, with little given back.
sounds: Anyway, enough about you. Let me tell you what happened with my sister.
You're so good at this. Nobody listens like you do.
I know you've got a lot on, but I really need you tonight.
That sounds hard. Anyway, mine was worse.
You always know what to say. I don't know how you cope.
I can't talk about your thing right now. I'm too stressed.
You're the only one I can tell all of this to.
nots: A friend going through a genuinely hard stretch needs more for a while, and reciprocity resuming once things stabilize is ordinary.
Someone with their own significant unmet needs may be unable rather than unwilling to give back.
What distinguishes the pattern is an imbalance that is stable across years rather than weeks.
A caring role you chose, such as supporting a sick relative or a person in recovery, where the imbalance is understood and agreed.
A therapist, counselor or helper who is paid for a one-sided relationship.
Different needs for talk: a more expressive friend who talks more, yet shows up for you in other ways.
compendium.why: Depletion accumulates so gradually that it registers as a personal failing, such as tiredness or low tolerance, rather than as the arithmetic of a relationship that never balances. You may blame yourself for running out of patience.

compendium.name: Information Control
compendium.what: Narrowing what someone reads, hears and learns, and who they talk to, so that one person's account becomes the main version of events available to them.
sounds: You don't need to read that, it's all lies.
Your sister doesn't understand our situation. Don't tell her about this.
I'll call the bank for you. You'll only get confused.
Where did you hear that? Who's been filling your head?
That doctor doesn't know us. Just ask me.
Don't bother with the group chat, they only stir things up.
Everything you need to know, I'll tell you.
nots: Warning someone about a source that really is unreliable, while leaving them free to look at it for themselves.
Someone who is simply uninformed and has no outside views to pass on, so is filtering nothing.
Limits on what young children watch or read, which loosen as the child grows.
A confidentiality rule at work that is disclosed to everyone, such as not discussing client files.
Taking over paperwork at your request, like a partner who handles the post while you recover from surgery and hands it back when you ask.
A friend who disagrees with an article you shared and says why.
compendium.why: A second opinion never reaches you, so a single account of events is all you have to reason with, and your doubts about it have nothing to be checked against.

compendium.name: Device Access Demands
compendium.what: Insisting on passwords, an unlocked phone or account logins as proof of trust, so that having a private space is read as a sign of hiding something.
sounds: If you have nothing to hide, you won't mind me looking.
Unlock it. Now.
Give me your password, or I'll assume the worst.
Why did you change your passcode?
Couples shouldn't have secrets from each other.
Hand over the phone while we talk.
I just need to check that you're being safe online.
nots: A mutually agreed, revocable arrangement, such as managing a young child's tablet or sharing a family account that either person can leave.
A disclosed institutional requirement applied to everyone, such as monitored work accounts with the policy in writing.
A streaming login, shared calendar or photo library that you both set up and either of you can end.
A one-off, like handing over a phone to show a specific message, with permission asked and the scope limited to that message.
Sharing a phone code with a trusted person while traveling, which you choose and undo.
compendium.why: Once saying no looks like guilt, privacy has to be defended instead of assumed. People can lose the ordinary sense that their messages, searches and private thoughts belong to them.

compendium.name: Enforcing Trivial Demands
compendium.what: Insisting on exact compliance with small, pointless-seeming rules, with a seriousness out of proportion to the stakes, until going along becomes routine.
sounds: No, the cups go handle-out. I've told you.
Do it again. Properly.
It's not about the towel, it's about listening.
Why can't you just do it the way I asked?
We do it my way in this house.
You walked in with your shoes on. Is that how little you care?
I said the lid faces left.
nots: A personal preference about how things are done, explained and flexible, which is ordinary fussiness and nothing more.
A rule with a function the person hasn't been told, like the food-safety order in a kitchen or a lab's labeling system.
High standards in a craft or role the person cares about, applied to themselves as much as to you.
A routine that helps someone with sensory needs or anxiety, which they explain and which is open to adjustment.
House rules agreed jointly, like a chore chart everybody wrote.
A family or cultural custom with a meaning everyone understands, like taking shoes off at the door.
compendium.why: When going along with petty rules becomes automatic, going along with big ones can feel like the same small step. The person also loses the ability to tell what truly matters to the other and what is just upkeep.

compendium.name: Boundary Testing
compendium.what: Crossing a stated or implied limit in small steps, where each step that goes unchallenged is followed by a slightly bigger one.
sounds: It's just a hug, relax.
I only borrowed it. You never mind.
Oh come on, one more drink won't hurt.
I know you said no calls after nine, but this was important.
You're making a big deal out of nothing.
I wasn't going to ask, but I'm already outside.
You didn't say anything last time.
nots: A one-off misjudgement with nothing following it, which is a mistake.
Someone unclear where the line sits who adjusts once told, and so has done exactly the right thing.
Good-faith negotiation about where a reasonable limit should sit, such as asking whether a rule can bend for a special occasion.
A toddler or teenager pressing on edges as part of growing up, who needs a steady reply rather than suspicion.
A new colleague who doesn't yet know the office habits and stops when told.
Different customs about closeness or timing, such as dropping in unannounced being normal in someone's family.
compendium.why: Since no single step seems worth a row, the line can move a long way without one clear moment to hold it. The person on the receiving end often feels the shift only afterwards, and wonders why they didn't say something sooner.

compendium.name: Velvet Glove Control
compendium.what: Narrowing someone's choices through warmth, concern and gentle persistence instead of force, so that the loss of their say is hard to see.
sounds: I just worry about you, that's all.
Let me handle it. You've got enough on your plate.
I only want what's best for you. You know that.
You don't have to decide anything. I've sorted it.
I'm not telling you what to do. I'd just be hurt if you went.
After everything I do for you, I'd think you'd listen.
I've already booked it. You'll thank me later.
Let's talk about it again tomorrow, shall we?
nots: Gentle guidance from someone who ultimately accepts a decision they disagree with, which is care.
Honest worry, said once, about a risky choice, followed by support for whatever you decide.
Help you asked for, such as someone running errands during an illness or a partner who handles the taxes by agreement.
A naturally soft-spoken person whose requests are easy to refuse and who doesn't mind when you do.
A professional carer or mentor advising within their role and accepting that you decide.
Someone who disagrees warmly and then comes along anyway.
compendium.why: With nothing harsh to point at, it is hard to say what is wrong, even to yourself. Choices can shrink while you are being reminded how lucky you are to be cared for.

compendium.name: Demonstrating Omnipotence
compendium.what: Showing off how much someone knows, controls or can reach in your life, until trying to act independently starts to look pointless.
sounds: I know you stopped at the pharmacy before work.
Funny, I was in your building today. Small world.
I had a quiet word with your manager. Don't worry about it.
You can't surprise me. People tell me everything.
Whatever you try, I'll hear about it before you've finished doing it.
I know people at that school, so I'll hear if anything is wrong.
A photo of you sent with no message, taken somewhere you did not know they were.
nots: Someone who truly has more information or contacts in one area and uses it openly to help, such as a relative who works at the hospital you are attending.
A coincidence with a plain explanation, like learning where you were from a friend you both know or from a post you shared yourself.
A well-connected person who mentions their network because it is part of who they are, with no change in how you act afterwards.
A parent or carer who knows details because the household shares a calendar and a family chat.
Boasting. Bragging about influence to everyone is self-presentation, and it differs from reach pointed at the choices of one person.
A supervisor who knows your schedule because that is what supervising your shifts involves.
compendium.why: Resistance can stop before anything has been tried, because it has already been made to look pointless. The loss is a choice you never test, and since nothing was tested, you may not notice that it was given up.

compendium.name: Forced Dependency
compendium.what: Arranging a relationship or setting so that one person cannot manage without the other's continued help, and keeping it that way.
sounds: Leave the money side to me. You'd only get it wrong.
Why would you need to learn to drive? I'm always here.
I'll book it for you. It's easier if I just do it.
You don't need to see the account. Everything is sorted.
I held on to your passport so it wouldn't get lost.
Don't bother with that course. What would you do with it?
A bank card kept in the other person's drawer, or an email login nobody else has.
nots: One partner handling the bills because they like spreadsheets and the other is happy to see the summary whenever they ask.
Reasonable reliance during an illness, a move, a new baby or a bereavement, with the shared aim of the person regaining their feet.
Someone who has decided they simply do not want to learn a task, and knows they could ask.
A carer who handles things for a person whose condition truly makes it unsafe to do them alone, with the person's input and review.
A teacher, mentor or professional who holds back information for a legitimate stage-by-stage reason and tells you how you will get access.
Cultural or generational family roles that both adults chose, with open access to the information involved.
compendium.why: The ability to cope alone is not so much lost as never allowed to grow, so staying becomes the only workable option and not a chosen one. Leaving or disagreeing then carries a practical cost that grows each year.

compendium.name: Golden Bars
compendium.what: Offering real comfort, money or status that comes with unspoken conditions, so that leaving or disagreeing means losing a good life.
sounds: Look at everything you would be giving up.
Most people would kill for what you have.
I give you a good life. All I ask is a little consideration.
After all I've provided, I think I can expect this.
You wouldn't last a month on your own salary.
Be sensible. Where else would you find this?
The cards, the house and the car are in my name, as you know.
nots: A generous partner or employer whose gifts and support would carry on through an argument.
Honest discussion of the trade-offs in any big decision, such as the cost of moving or the loss of a salary, raised by both people openly.
A person who values comfort and says so, as one factor among many in a mutual decision.
A gift given with no expectation, even if the person later feels hurt about how it was received.
Reasonable terms of a job, such as a company flat that goes with the role, which are written down and apply to everyone in it.
Gratitude. Feeling thankful for what a person has provided is not evidence that you are being held.
compendium.why: Comfort turns into an argument against leaving that has nothing to do with whether the arrangement is sound, and describing the situation to anyone else makes it sound enviable. Your unhappiness can seem ungrateful, even to you.

compendium.name: Manufactured Scarcity
compendium.what: Claiming that a chance, a person or a deal is about to disappear, so that fear of losing it replaces careful thought.
sounds: There are only two spots left, and I can't hold yours past tonight.
If you leave this room without signing, the price goes up tomorrow.
I've got three other people interested, so I need to know by five.
I'm not going to wait around forever. It's now or never.
A message from a landlord saying 'multiple viewings, decide today' with no other details.
This door will not open again. You'll regret it.
A friend says 'everyone in the group has already committed', before you have heard the details.
nots: A true deadline, such as an application closing date, a sale with a posted end, or a flight leaving, which can be confirmed on the organizer's own page.
Someone accurately describing real stakes, such as a job offer that expires on Friday, and being willing to give you the written terms.
A friend or relative who feels strongly and says 'I hope you will do it', without a clock attached.
A seller who says honestly that an item is the last one in stock, and lets you check.
Your own fear of missing out, which can arise with no one applying pressure.
A person who sets out their own limit, such as 'I need an answer by the weekend to plan', which is a request about their own planning and not a threat about your options.
compendium.why: Fear of losing the opportunity does the evaluating, and by the time there is room to think properly the decision has already been made. People can end up committed to money, housing, jobs or relationships they would have weighed very differently with a week.

compendium.name: Time Theft
compendium.what: Repeatedly spending another person's time carelessly, through lateness, waiting and canceled plans, in a way that treats their hours as worth less than one's own.
sounds: Just wait there, I'll be ten minutes. (Ninety minutes later.)
Oh, you had plans? Cancel them, this is more important.
I can't give you a time, just keep your evening free.
You don't have anywhere else to be, do you?
It's only an hour. Why are you making a fuss?
My time is valuable. You can fit around me.
Messages that say 'on my way' repeatedly, with no arrival.
nots: Occasional lateness from traffic, illness or a crisis, mentioned honestly and apologized for, with a change next time.
A person who is disorganised with everyone, including their own appointments, and who is not singling you out.
Real unpredictability in shift work, caring duties or emergency jobs, which affects everyone close to them and which they are open about.
A genuine difference in how each of you views punctuality, which you can name and agree on.
A culture or workplace where meetings begin when people arrive, and everyone expects that.
Someone lacking attention to time for reasons such as ADHD or anxiety, who works at it and tells you when they cannot manage.
compendium.why: Hours are lost that cannot be recovered, and the message carried in the losing of them, that this person's time is not worth planning around, is absorbed long before it is ever named. Over months it can wear down your sense of what you are allowed to expect.

compendium.name: Deflection
compendium.what: Steering a conversation away from the issue that was raised, so the concern never gets a direct answer.
sounds: Did you cancel the appointment? / Why are you always checking up on me?
Can we talk about this later? (said again each time, with no later arriving)
Why are you bringing this up now?
That's not the point. The point is how you brought it up.
Speaking of which, did you ever call your mother back? (in the middle of your question)
Here we go again. You always have to start something.
When you ask about last month's missed payment, the talk turns to something you said at Christmas.
Three subjects in two minutes, and each time you go back to your first point, a fourth begins.
nots: Someone overwhelmed who asks for a pause and does come back, or a person who misheard the question and answered something nearby. Dealing with a truly urgent related matter first is also fine, so long as the original topic is picked up again.
A clarifying question such as 'Which time do you mean?', after which your answer leads to theirs.
A group conversation where tangents are normal and no one's question outranks another's.
Weariness with a long-running argument: 'not this again' can be plain exhaustion and not a way of escaping the subject.
A busy, fast-moving meeting that touches many items briefly and has a clear time for follow-up.
compendium.why: The original concern never gets a direct reply, so it stays open while the conversation ends looking as though it happened. The person who raised it is left unsure whether they were heard at all.

compendium.name: Apology Without Repair
compendium.what: An apology that is offered but followed by no change in behavior, so the same harm returns and the apology closes the matter each time.
sounds: I'm sorry, okay? What more do you want from me?
I said I was sorry. How many times do I have to say it?
I'm so sorry. I hate myself when I do this. (which leaves you comforting them)
I already apologized for that last month. Why are you still going on about it?
It won't happen again, said for the fourth time about the same thing.
A text reading 'Sorry for everything' that names no action.
A tearful apology, a nice dinner, and the same late arrival the following week.
nots: A sincere apology followed by imperfect effort. Change is rarely instant and rarely a straight line.
Someone who apologizes well but has a real skill gap, with money or time, and needs a plan more than willpower.
One relapse followed by renewed effort, which is not a closed loop.
A person whose follow-through is affected by something like ADHD or depression, who is open about it and working on it.
An apology for something that cannot be undone, where no further repair is possible.
An apology you both agree is enough: 'that's all I needed'.
compendium.why: Each apology closes the incident without changing anything, so the same harm can recur while, on paper, it has been dealt with every time. The person on the receiving end is left holding a record of apologies and no change.

compendium.name: Forced Forgiveness
compendium.what: Pressing someone to forgive or move on before the harm has been acknowledged or made right, so forgiveness is demanded in place of repair.
sounds: Can we just move past this?
It's been long enough. You need to let it go.
Forgiveness is what God asks of us, and you're holding on.
He's family. Life's too short to hold grudges.
I've said I'm sorry. Now you have to forgive me. That's how it works.
Everyone else has moved on. Why can't you?
If you really cared about this family, you'd shake his hand at the wedding.
nots: A mutual decision to move forward after real acknowledgment has happened. That is repair, not pressure.
Someone who processes conflict quickly and does not ask others to match their pace.
Family or cultural norms about not dwelling, which are not avoidance by default.
Your own wish to forgive and let go, which is a choice and not a pressure.
A mediator or counselor who raises forgiveness as an option after both sides have been heard. An invitation is not a demand.
A friend who says 'I hope you can find peace with this someday' and requires nothing.
compendium.why: Resolution is claimed before acknowledgment, so the harm stays unprocessed. Any further mention of it then becomes the new problem, and the person who was hurt carries the extra task of looking forgiving.

compendium.name: Plausible Deniability
compendium.what: Acting in ways that can always be explained as concern, policy or accident, so no single incident can be called harmful without the accuser sounding unfair.
sounds: I was only worried about you. That's why I read your messages.
It's just policy. My hands are tied.
I didn't mean it that way. You're reading into it.
It was a joke. Where's your sense of humor?
I was just being honest.
I never told you not to go. I just said I'd be upset.
I must have forgotten to tell you about the change to your shifts.
Nobody said you couldn't. We just thought it would look bad.
nots: People do follow policy and do worry about others. Often the innocent explanation is simply the true one.
Someone careful and honest can sound identical to someone producing cover. One ambiguous incident cannot separate the two, which is why this belongs at the level of a pattern.
Honest mistakes that happen to cluster, such as a disorganized manager whose errors hit everyone.
Tact and indirectness. Hinting to avoid conflict is the polite norm in many families and cultures.
An understaffed office where problems come from chaos and not from any design.
compendium.why: Every incident comes with a fair-sounding explanation, so raising any one of them can make the person raising it look unreasonable. The pattern can only be described by pointing at things that, taken separately, look like nothing.

compendium.name: Feigned Ignorance
compendium.what: Acting as if you do not know or cannot follow something, so that a responsibility is dropped or a hard conversation is put off.
sounds: "Wait, what promise? I honestly don't remember us agreeing to that."
"Can you explain the due date again? I'm not sure I ever saw it."
"I had no idea that was a rule here." (said about a rule they signed off on)
"I didn't realize that was a problem." (said after the third conversation about it)
"You'll have to walk me through what you mean. I'm lost."
A blank look and "huh?" when the topic turns to their share of the work, followed by easy chat about something else.
nots: Ordinary forgetting, which is strongest in busy or sleepless stretches and hits many subjects, including ones that matter to the person.
A real gap in knowledge on a hard topic, such as taxes, a legal form or a medical term, where confusion matches difficulty and not convenience.
Someone who was truly not in the room, never saw the message, or got a different version of the plan.
A person who asks for a second explanation, listens, and then acts on it. Asking twice is not evasion.
Cultural or language differences that make an instruction land differently than it was meant.
compendium.why: When a person seems not to understand, nothing can be settled, because the shared basis for settling it is missing. Whoever raised the issue ends up explaining it again and again instead of getting an answer.

compendium.name: Victim Role Reversal
compendium.what: Presenting oneself as the injured party when asked to answer for harm, so that sympathy and comforting move away from the person who was actually hurt.
sounds: "After everything I've done, this is how I'm treated? I'm the one who's been hurt here."
"Do you have any idea how hard this has been for me?" (after you raised what they did)
"I'm the one everyone piles onto. Nobody ever asks how I'm doing."
