codex_completed.name: Cognitive Warfare
codex_completed.detectability_note: This tool cannot establish this from pasted text at all. It is included for literacy only, so you can learn to recognize the concept — not as something this tool detects, scores, or flags.
codex_completed.core_meaning: Efforts to wear down a population's ability to think clearly, trust shared facts, and reach agreement, by working on beliefs and attention.
codex_completed.short_definition: Efforts to wear down a population's ability to think clearly, trust shared facts, and reach agreement, by working on beliefs and attention.
codex_completed.expanded_definition: Cognitive warfare is a term used in security circles for campaigns aimed at how a society thinks, not at its buildings or machines. Instead of persuading people of one claim, such campaigns can aim to leave them tired, suspicious of each other, and unable to settle on what is true. The word is contested and sometimes overused. Real societies also fall into confusion and distrust without any outside plan.
codex_completed.plain_language_summary: A campaign that tries to leave a whole society confused, divided and unable to agree on facts, instead of winning people to one side.
codex_completed.why_this_matters: What is attacked is a group's ability to reason together. The damage can show up as exhaustion, mutual distrust, and an inability to agree on anything long enough to act on it, which weakens people whichever side they are on.
what_it_is: A strategy aimed at a population's attention, beliefs and trust rather than at its physical resources.
Often described as working through many small, repeated pushes, and not through one big lie.
Spread across news, social platforms, rumors, humor and ordinary conversation, which makes the source hard to see.
Judged by its effect on a group: confusion, cynicism, and the feeling that nothing can be known.
A contested label. Researchers and officials do not all define it the same way.
what_it_sounds_like: A flood of conflicting accounts of the same event, so that people give up deciding which is right.
Posts insisting that 'everyone lies, so nothing can be trusted'.
Neighbors who once talked now avoid a subject because every conversation turns hostile.
Emotional stories, shared widely, that make an ordinary group of people seem like enemies.
Sudden bursts of outrage about a topic that most people had never discussed before.
Trusted institutions and local reporters described again and again as fools or frauds.
what_it_is_not: A society arguing with itself. People disagree, polarize and lose trust for their own reasons, such as economic strain, real grievances and poor governance.
Ordinary advertising or political persuasion, which tries to win agreement openly and for a stated side.
A single rumor or hoax, which is misinformation, not necessarily a campaign.
Public diplomacy and openly labeled state media, which tell you who is speaking.
A convenient explanation for any social problem. Blaming a foreign adversary for domestic dysfunction is itself a familiar political move.
this_may_be_it_when: Independent researchers or journalists have documented a coordinated effort with an identified sponsor.
Confusing, contradictory messages push in several opposed directions at once about the same event.
Content seems built to inflame mutual contempt among groups instead of persuading anyone.
The same themes recur across unconnected platforms, languages and communities.
The effect lasts after the original claims are debunked, leaving only a vague distrust.
this_may_not_be_it_when: The disagreement has a clear local cause, such as a closed factory, a contested law or a recent scandal.
The conflict grows from messages people sent in their own voices, to people they know.
The only evidence is that the situation feels chaotic.
The claim of outside manipulation comes mainly from a side that gains from blaming outsiders.
No sponsor, method or documentation has been shown, only a mood.
innocent_or_ordinary_possibilities: Fast news cycles overwhelm everyone and can feel like deliberate confusion even when nobody planned it.
Sincere people on opposite sides can hold sharply different views of the same facts.
Algorithms that reward engagement can spread angry content without any central plan.
common_false_positives: A heated election season in which real voters are genuinely angry.
A viral hoax started by a single bored person.
A community split over a local issue, where the argument is about something real.
discernment_questions: Is there documented evidence of who is behind this, or only a feeling that someone must be?
Does this content want me to believe one thing, or to give up on believing anything?
Am I being nudged to see my neighbors as enemies?
Would I still find this alarming if it came from a side I agree with?
Do reliable, independent sources describe the same events, even if they disagree about the meaning?
less_concerning_if: The dispute has identifiable local causes and people still talk across the divide.
Independent reporting explains the confusion without needing a hidden hand.
People involved can still agree on some basic facts, even while disagreeing on policy.
more_concerning_if: Documented coordination with a named sponsor sits behind the confusion.
Contempt and exhaustion spread through a community faster than any single issue could explain.
People start to say that no source at all can be believed.
pattern_over_time_signs: Trust in many different institutions and outlets falls together, not one at a time.
The topics change but the effect stays the same: more suspicion, less cooperation.
Ordinary conversations get harder, with friends and relatives avoiding certain subjects.
Debunked claims return in new forms, and each return finds fewer people willing to check.
codex_completed.repair_check: Recovery looks like shared facts rebuilt slowly: institutions that show their sources and admit errors, and neighbors who can disagree and still talk. A louder counter-campaign, or an accusation that only the other side is manipulated, repeats the damage.
codex_completed.boundary_respect_check: Slow down and see what the content does to you. If it wants an instant reaction, a side picked, or a verdict that nobody can be believed, that urgency is worth questioning. Material that survives a pause and a second source is safer to take seriously.
codex_completed.psychological_mechanism: People rely on shared facts and a sense that others are reasonable in order to cooperate. Repeated overload, contradiction and provocation can tend to tire attention, make skepticism feel like safety, and turn disagreement into personal hostility. Once trust drops, even accurate information has a harder time being believed.
codex_completed.possible_impact_on_receiver: People describe news fatigue, a feeling that everything is spin, and rising irritation with relatives or neighbors over topics they once discussed calmly. Some withdraw from public life altogether. Others become sure that everyone who disagrees is a dupe, which can leave them lonelier and more easily provoked.

response_options.soft_clarification: When a topic is getting heated, ask the other person what they have actually read and where it came from, and offer the sources you used.
response_options.firm_boundary: Choose a small number of sources you can check and trust, and decline to react to content from accounts you cannot place.
response_options.disengagement: Take a break from feeds that leave you angry and exhausted. Rest is a legitimate response, not surrender.
response_options.support_seeking: Talk with someone from the other side of a divide in person, about something other than the dispute, to remember they are a real neighbor.
response_options.workplace_or_professional: If you work in education, journalism, public service or platform integrity, document what you observe and use your organization's channels for reporting suspected coordinated activity.

codex_completed.boundary_script: "Is this trying to convince me of something specific, or just make me angry and tired? Who made it, where did it start, and can I find a second source before I react?"
codex_completed.safety_note: Reading contested content is not a personal danger, but campaigns of this kind can spill into harassment of named people or into pressure to act at once. If you see threats or personal details being spread, save examples, report them to the platform, and alert the people affected. If you feel unsafe, contact local emergency services.
misuse_warning: Calling any disagreement 'cognitive warfare' can turn a political opponent into an enemy agent. The term needs documented evidence, and not just a dislike of someone's views.
Using it to explain away every bad mood in a society hides real grievances that people have a right to raise.
codex_completed.how_to_distinguish_from_related: PSYOP Message Framing concerns how a single message is built to move a particular audience, and cognitive warfare is the wider effort to degrade a whole population's reasoning. Strategic Deception targets an adversary's decisions about plans and capabilities. Agent of Influence works through one credible person. What sets this apart is its target: a society's shared sense of what is true.

codex_completed.name: Cyber Manipulation Operations (CMOs)
codex_completed.detectability_note: This tool cannot establish this from pasted text at all. It is included for literacy only, so you can learn to recognize the concept — not as something this tool detects, scores, or flags.
codex_completed.core_meaning: Quietly changing, inventing or deleting data inside a system, so that people make decisions based on records they believe are real.
codex_completed.short_definition: Quietly changing, inventing or deleting data inside a system, so that people make decisions based on records they believe are real.
codex_completed.expanded_definition: Cyber manipulation operations, sometimes called CMOs, are intrusions whose goal is not to steal information but to alter it. A balance, a record, a sensor reading or a message is changed, and the people relying on it act on false figures without knowing. Nothing appears stolen and nothing appears broken. This is a forensic finding made by specialists, and it is not something to conclude from one number that looks wrong.
codex_completed.plain_language_summary: Instead of stealing information, someone secretly changes it, so the people who rely on it make choices based on figures that are quietly wrong.
codex_completed.why_this_matters: Nothing appears stolen and nothing appears broken, so decisions carry on being made confidently on figures that are quietly wrong. By the time anyone notices, the harm may already be done and trust in the records themselves is damaged.
what_it_is: Tampering with the contents of records, such as balances, results, logs, readings or messages, rather than taking a copy.
Aimed at the decisions people make, not at the data as such.
Meant to go unnoticed, since a change that is detected loses its effect.
Found in finance, public records, health, industry and news, anywhere people rely on stored figures.
Established by specialists examining logs and backups, not by how a number looks.
what_it_sounds_like: Two official systems that should agree show different totals, and nobody can say why.
A published figure is quietly revised, and the revision history cannot be explained.
Records show an action no one remembers taking.
Audit logs have gaps for the exact period in question.
Statements to customers contain errors that match no known software fault.
An organization announces that it is checking whether data was 'altered', and not just accessed.
what_it_is_not: A software bug, a botched migration, or a typing mistake. Data corrupts through ordinary error far more often than through intrusion.
A number you personally find surprising. A discrepancy is a reason to investigate, not a conclusion.
Data theft or a breach where information is copied, which is a different harm.
A planned correction, in which an organization changes a record and documents why.
Routine rounding, timing differences, or two systems measuring things differently.
this_may_be_it_when: Specialists examining the system find unauthorized changes to stored records.
Backups and live records disagree in a way that points to deliberate edits.
The altered figures consistently favor one outcome.
Access logs show someone with no reason to be in the system changing entries.
An organization confirms that records were altered without authorization.
this_may_not_be_it_when: The error is explained by a known software fault or a data-entry mistake.
The numbers differ because the two sources define the figure differently.
The only evidence is a hunch that something is off.
A correction has been logged, with a reason and a name attached.
The discrepancy disappears once the record is rechecked.
innocent_or_ordinary_possibilities: Rushed updates, merged databases and old formats produce wrong figures without anyone meaning harm.
Staff sometimes fix a record and forget to log it.
Delays in syncing between systems can make totals disagree for a while.
common_false_positives: A bank statement that shows a pending charge differently from the final one.
A dashboard that lags a few hours behind the source.
A spreadsheet in which a formula was broken by someone's innocent edit.
discernment_questions: Is there a documented, ordinary explanation for the difference?
Can the figure be checked against a second, independent record?
Has anyone qualified examined the system, or is this still a guess?
Who would gain if this particular number were wrong?
Is the organization willing to explain what it found and what it does not yet know?
less_concerning_if: The discrepancy has a simple explanation and is fixed once the cause is found.
Independent records agree with the figure you were first given.
The organization is open about the checks it ran and what they showed.
more_concerning_if: The errors are consistent in direction and cannot be explained by software or human mistakes.
Logs, backups or records are missing or incomplete for the period in question.
The organization is slow to check, or discourages questions about the figures.
pattern_over_time_signs: Small discrepancies keep appearing in the same type of record and are repeatedly written off.
Decisions based on the affected figures turn out badly more often than expected.
People start keeping their own copies because they no longer trust the official ones.
Review after review reveals changes nobody can attribute to a person or process.
codex_completed.repair_check: Real recovery means restoring records from trusted backups, telling affected people what changed, and showing how future changes will be logged and reviewed. A bare statement that everything is fine, with no account of what was checked, does not rebuild trust.
codex_completed.boundary_respect_check: When you ask an organization to confirm a figure against an independent record, notice the answer. A willingness to check and to say what the check showed is a good sign. Defensiveness, or an answer that only repeats the original number, tells you less.
codex_completed.psychological_mechanism: Official records and automatic systems are usually treated as neutral and rarely re-checked. Altered data can exploit that default trust: a confident decision made on a false figure feels just like a sound one. Doubt arrives late, and once it does it can spread well beyond the records that were actually changed.
codex_completed.possible_impact_on_receiver: People describe confusion and anger at discovering that a decision they made in good faith rested on a false figure, along with lingering suspicion of systems they used to trust. Some say they now keep personal copies of important records and check them more often.

response_options.soft_clarification: If a figure looks wrong, ask the organization to confirm it against a second record and tell you how the check was done.
response_options.firm_boundary: Decline to act on a high-stakes number until it has been confirmed by an independent source or by a second system.
response_options.disengagement: If a service keeps giving you inconsistent records, move important dealings to channels you can document, and keep your own dated copies.
response_options.support_seeking: Report a suspected problem to the organization's security or records team, and ask a consumer protection service or a lawyer about your options.
response_options.workplace_or_professional: If you work with sensitive records, report anomalies through your organization's incident process quickly, keep a dated note of what you saw, and avoid changing anything that could be evidence.

codex_completed.boundary_script: "This number doesn't match what I expected. Before I act on it, can it be confirmed against a second record, and is there an ordinary explanation that has been checked?"
codex_completed.safety_note: A wrong number is not a threat to your physical safety. It becomes serious when altered records affect medicine, money, housing or legal status. In those cases contact the provider or agency directly, keep copies of what you have, and ask a legal aid service or consumer protection office for help.
misuse_warning: Treating every odd figure as sabotage can shut down honest error-checking and make people accuse colleagues or officials without evidence.
Claiming that results were secretly altered, with no forensic finding, can wrongly destroy trust in records that are accurate.
codex_completed.how_to_distinguish_from_related: Strategic Deception misleads an adversary through coordinated concealment and misdirection across many channels, while a data-altering operation changes what a specific system holds. Strategic Leaking releases real information at a chosen moment, whereas this alters the information itself. PSYOP Message Framing shapes how a message is received; this corrupts the record that decisions depend on.
codex_completed.detection_notes: Not matched or scored. Pasted personal text cannot establish an institutional- or societal-scale pattern — that requires independent, corroborated, documented evidence at a completely different scale.

codex_completed.name: Adversarial Machine Learning
codex_completed.detectability_note: This tool cannot establish this from pasted text at all. It is included for literacy only, so you can learn to recognize the concept — not as something this tool detects, scores, or flags.
codex_completed.core_meaning: Crafting the data an AI system learns from or reads so that it gives wrong or manipulated answers, a risk to filters, fraud checks and screening software.
codex_completed.short_definition: Crafting the data an AI system learns from or reads so that it gives wrong or manipulated answers, a risk to filters, fraud checks and screening software.
codex_completed.expanded_definition: Adversarial machine learning is the study of how AI systems can be pushed into mistakes by inputs designed for that purpose, and of how to defend against it. For ordinary people the point is simple: a filter, a fraud check or a screening tool can be fooled, and it will still return a confident answer. Strange or wrong outputs are far more often ordinary limitations than attacks, and this entry gives no detail on any method.
codex_completed.plain_language_summary: AI systems can be fooled by inputs made to mislead them, so a confident answer from a filter or screening tool is not always a correct one.
codex_completed.why_this_matters: The systems people are told to rely on, such as filters, fraud checks and screening tools, return confident answers, and the person affected often has no way to see why. If such a system has been misled, the error can land on someone who did nothing.
what_it_is: An attempt to make an AI system misread, misjudge or misclassify what it is given.
A concern for any automated decision tool, such as spam filters, fraud flags, content moderation, and screening software.
A field of research as well as a threat, since defenders study it to make systems safer.
Usually invisible to the person on the receiving end, who sees only the system's answer.
Distinct from ordinary AI error, which happens without anyone trying to cause it.
what_it_sounds_like: A message that clearly looks like a scam passes an automated filter and lands in your inbox.
A harmless account or document is flagged and blocked, with no explanation you can understand.
An application is rejected by an automated screen and nobody can say which factor decided it.
A tool that has behaved sensibly for months suddenly gives odd answers on a certain topic.
A researcher publishes a report showing that a particular AI product can be misled by certain inputs.
A company announces it has found that a system's results were being steered.
what_it_is_not: Everyday AI mistakes. Models break on unusual inputs, carry the biases of their training data, and drift as the world changes. A wrong or strange output is far more likely a limitation than an attack.
A system making a decision you dislike but that follows its stated rules.
Normal reports from security researchers who test systems with permission in order to fix them.
A human error in how a system was set up or who configured it.
Honest users who simply phrase things in unexpected ways.
this_may_be_it_when: The company or independent researchers confirm that a system was fed misleading inputs.
The same oddly wrong result appears repeatedly and only for inputs with something unusual in common.
A cluster of bad outcomes coincides with a change in the data the system was learning from.
The wrong answers consistently favor one outside party.
The organization running the system has publicly acknowledged and described the problem.
this_may_not_be_it_when: The error is occasional and varies at random, which is typical of ordinary model limits.
The system was recently updated or retrained and results shifted for known reasons.
The only evidence is that the answer seems unfair or surprising.
The tool was used outside what it was built for.
A person can review and correct the result when asked.
innocent_or_ordinary_possibilities: AI tools make mistakes with unusual wording, photos or accents even when nobody is trying to trick them.
Training data can be incomplete or skewed, producing consistent errors without any attacker.
Systems drift as language, scams and habits change, so once-good performance fades.
common_false_positives: A chatbot that gives a wrong fact with confidence.
A photo filter that misidentifies an object in poor light.
A spam filter that misses one new kind of scam message.
discernment_questions: Is there a human who can review this decision if I ask?
Has the organization or an independent researcher explained what went wrong?
Is this a one-off error, or a repeated, consistent one?
Am I treating the system's confidence as proof of correctness?
What other evidence do I have, apart from the system's answer?
less_concerning_if: A person reviews the automated result and corrects it without fuss.
The error is rare, random, and fixed after you report it.
The organization explains how the tool is tested and monitored.
more_concerning_if: An automated tool decides something about your money, job, housing, or legal status, and nobody can explain or review it.
The same type of mistake keeps hurting the same group of people.
The organization cannot or will not say how the system is checked for tampering.
pattern_over_time_signs: An error that was fixed returns in a slightly different form.
Reports of the same odd failure collect from many unconnected people.
The tool's results grow less trustworthy after some change in what it takes in.
Appeals are refused with the same answer, with no human looking at your case.
codex_completed.repair_check: Accountability would mean the operator telling affected people what went wrong, correcting individual decisions made on bad outputs, and showing how the system is now tested. A quiet fix with no account to those affected leaves the earlier decisions standing.
codex_completed.boundary_respect_check: Ask for a human review of any automated decision that matters, and note how it is received. A prompt, plain explanation and a real second look is a good sign. A reply that repeats the system's result as if it were final is a poor one.
codex_completed.psychological_mechanism: A computer seems neutral, fast and consistent, so its answers often get the benefit of the doubt. That trust can make an automated error harder to challenge than a human one. Opaque results also leave the affected person unsure where to push back, and many simply accept the outcome.
codex_completed.possible_impact_on_receiver: People describe frustration at being refused or flagged by a system nobody can explain, a sense of helplessness in appeals, and fresh distrust of automated tools. Some become wary of every confident AI answer, while others feel pressure to doubt their own judgment against the machine's.

response_options.soft_clarification: Ask the organization in plain words how a decision was reached and whether a person reviewed it, and request the answer in writing.
response_options.firm_boundary: Decline to treat an automated result as final for anything important, and ask for a human decision-maker to look at your case.
response_options.disengagement: If a tool keeps giving you doubtful answers, stop relying on it for important matters and use a second source or a person.
response_options.support_seeking: Take an unexplained automated decision to a consumer protection office, an advocacy group or a legal aid service, with copies of what you were told.
response_options.workplace_or_professional: If you work with automated tools, log odd results with dates and examples, report them to whoever maintains the system, and keep a human check on high-stakes outputs.

codex_completed.boundary_script: "This result came from an automated system, and a confident answer is not the same as a correct one. Can a person review it, and what else do I have that supports or contradicts it?"
codex_completed.safety_note: An odd AI result is rarely a personal danger. It becomes serious if an automated tool wrongly affects your money, housing, job, health care or legal standing. In that case ask for human review in writing, keep copies, and contact a legal aid service or consumer protection office.
misuse_warning: Blaming every strange AI output on an attack can excuse real design flaws and hide the ordinary biases and limits that cause most errors.
Accusing a specific person or company of tampering with a model, with no evidence, is a serious claim that can do real harm.
codex_completed.how_to_distinguish_from_related: Strategic Leaking releases real information at a chosen moment, while this entry concerns misleading an AI tool so that its judgments go wrong. Strategic Deception is a broad campaign to mislead an adversary's decisions through many channels. PSYOP Message Framing is crafted to move human audiences, whereas this entry is about fooling a machine's reading of its input.

codex_completed.name: Milieu Control
codex_completed.detectability_note: This tool cannot establish this from pasted text at all. It is included for literacy only, so you can learn to recognize the concept — not as something this tool detects, scores, or flags.
codex_completed.core_meaning: A group's tight control over what members can read, hear and discuss and whom they can see, so the group becomes their only source of information.
codex_completed.short_definition: A group's tight control over what members can read, hear and discuss and whom they can see, so the group becomes their only source of information.
codex_completed.expanded_definition: Milieu control means a group manages the information and the relationships around its members. It can be formal, such as banned books or rules about who may be contacted, or informal, such as steady pressure to spend all free time with fellow members. Robert Lifton, who studied thought reform, listed it among the features of totalistic groups. Wanting focus or privacy is normal. It becomes a pattern once outside contact, news and doubts are discouraged, reported or punished, and a member has nothing else to test the group's claims against.
codex_completed.plain_language_summary: The group decides what you may read, hear and say, and who you may talk to, until its version of the world is the only one you can reach.
codex_completed.why_this_matters: With reading, contact and conversation all bounded by the group, there is no outside view left to compare anything against, including the question of whether the boundary itself is reasonable.
what_it_is: Rules, spoken or unspoken, about which books, websites, news and media members may use.
Limits on who a member may call, visit or live near, often with family and old friends described as a bad influence.
A calendar so full of meetings, work and service that little time is left for anyone outside.
Members expected to report on each other's contacts, reading or doubts.
Seen in religious groups, political movements, self-improvement programs, communes and close-knit organizations, though most of those do not work this way.
what_it_sounds_like: Your family doesn't understand the work we're doing. Maybe give them some distance for now.
We don't read outside material here. It only confuses people.
Anyone you talk to outside should be mentioned to your leader first.
Those websites are written by people who hate us.
You don't need other friends. You have all of us.
Phones go in the box for the retreat, and the retreat keeps getting extended.
what_it_is_not: Communities of every kind have shared practices, retreats and times of deliberate focus, and choosing to spend most of your time among people who share your commitments is ordinary. The question is whether outside contact and information can resume without penalty.
A silent retreat or monastery that people enter by choice, with a known end date and a way to call home.
A school or workplace that limits phones during working hours.
Parents guiding what a young child watches and reads.
A close family or circle of friends that simply prefers one another's company.
A group that criticizes outside media in the open while members stay free to read it.
this_may_be_it_when: Members who read or contact outsiders have to hide it, or get reported by others.
Former members and relatives are described as enemies, and speaking to them is discouraged.
Outside news reaches members only after leaders have interpreted it.
Phones, mail or travel need permission, and permission is often refused.
A question about the rules draws suspicion about the asker's loyalty.
this_may_not_be_it_when: Members come and go and keep ordinary friendships outside.
Criticism of the group can be read and discussed openly.
A long stretch of time away brings no penalty or interrogation on return.
A restriction has a stated, limited purpose, such as a retreat, and ends when it does.
Relatives are welcome at events and can reach members directly.
innocent_or_ordinary_possibilities: A demanding season, such as a training program or a harvest, can leave little time for friends.
Some faith traditions encourage simple living or limited media, and members choose it gladly.
A new member may drop old habits eagerly, with nobody asking them to.
common_false_positives: A boarding school or military academy with posted phone rules and scheduled family calls.
A group that recommends its own reading list and says other books are welcome too.
A new job or a move that crowds out old routines without anyone intending it.
discernment_questions: Could you contact an old friend or relative tomorrow and speak freely, with nobody asking what was said?
Can you read criticism of the group in full without being asked to justify why?
Does anyone track whom you talk to or what you read?
When you voice a doubt, who finds out about it?
Can you hear from people who left in their own words, or only through the group's description of them?
less_concerning_if: Members can step away for weeks and return to a warm welcome.
Leaders say openly that outside views are fine and members act on it.
Contact limits are short, explained and chosen by the member.
more_concerning_if: Spending time with outsiders brings shaming, extra duties or loss of standing.
Members lack their own money, phone or transport and cannot reach anyone without help from the group.
Members who drift away are cut off from everyone still inside.
pattern_over_time_signs: Your circle of friends outside the group shrinks, one canceled plan at a time.
You stop reading or watching things you used to enjoy without quite deciding to.
You catch yourself describing relatives with the group's words for them.
Doubts feel unsafe to say aloud to anyone, even a person you trust.
codex_completed.repair_check: Real change would show as open doors: contact rules lifted, outside reading no longer questioned, former members heard directly instead of described. A statement about openness, with the same permission gate still in place, changes nothing a member can feel.
codex_completed.boundary_respect_check: Notice what follows an afternoon with an outside friend or an outside article. Curiosity from the group points one way. Questions about who knew, or a cooler reception afterward, point the other.
codex_completed.psychological_mechanism: When one group supplies nearly all of a person's information, friendships and daily routine, it can become the standard for what seems normal. Without other voices to compare against, small restrictions tend to feel reasonable, and doubts can start to feel like personal failings. Each step often seems minor on its own.
codex_completed.possible_impact_on_receiver: People describe losing touch with friends and family, feeling unable to judge whether the group's claims hold up, and shame about wanting outside contact. After a long time inside, some describe feeling lost in ordinary life, unsure how to rebuild relationships or what to trust.

response_options.soft_clarification: Ask a plain question in the group: 'Is it all right if I keep up with my sister?' How the question is received tells you a good deal.
response_options.firm_boundary: State a small, specific limit and keep it: 'I'm going to keep reading what I like, and I'd rather not talk about it.'
response_options.disengagement: Take a walk, a nap or a quiet hour alone when pressure builds, and keep one steady contact outside the group informed of how you are.
response_options.support_seeking: Reach someone who knew you before, or a counselor who understands high-control groups, and say what daily life is like in your own words.
response_options.workplace_or_professional: If a workplace program or training limits contact and outside information, ask for the policy in writing and keep copies where the organization cannot see them.

codex_completed.boundary_script: "One afternoon a week is for my own friends and my own reading. It has nothing to do with how I feel about this group. It is just something I need."
codex_completed.safety_note: Warning signs include being watched, having your phone, money or documents held, being told what will happen to people who question, or fear of what follows contact with family. Decisions about leaving are best made privately, with an experienced advocate, a counselor who knows high-control groups, or a trusted person outside. If you are in immediate danger, contact emergency services.
misuse_warning: Calling a tight-knit congregation, team or family a controlling group because it is close or devout mistakes closeness for control. The test is whether outside contact is penalized.
Telling someone their group is controlling their world can push them to defend it. A question about how free they feel usually lands better than a label.
codex_completed.how_to_distinguish_from_related: Doctrine Over Person is about what a member is taught to think of their own experience, whereas milieu control concerns what reaches them to begin with. Sacred Science makes the doctrine unquestionable; milieu control makes sure the questions never arrive. Bounded Choice describes how choices come to feel free. Here the matter is simply who may talk to whom.

codex_completed.name: Mystical Manipulation
codex_completed.detectability_note: This tool cannot establish this from pasted text at all. It is included for literacy only, so you can learn to recognize the concept — not as something this tool detects, scores, or flags.
codex_completed.core_meaning: Arranging events that look spontaneous or divine, such as visions, healings or signs, to persuade members that a leader holds special spiritual authority.
codex_completed.short_definition: Arranging events that look spontaneous or divine, such as visions, healings or signs, to persuade members that a leader holds special spiritual authority.
codex_completed.expanded_definition: Mystical manipulation is when experiences presented as spontaneous or divinely sent were in fact arranged by leadership, then used as proof of the leader's special connection. Robert Lifton listed it among his criteria for thought reform, and it is separate from belief itself. Prepared settings, music and ritual are ordinary in worship. The concern is an event staged in secret and presented as chance, so that members treat it as evidence and feel they cannot question the person who presided over it.
codex_completed.plain_language_summary: A moving or miraculous moment is quietly set up, then presented as an unplanned sign that the leader is chosen, so members stop questioning that leader.
codex_completed.why_this_matters: An experience read as evidence of something greater is very hard to reconsider later, and the authority it lends to whoever presided over it is correspondingly hard to question.
what_it_is: An event described as unplanned, such as a vision, a healing or a perfectly timed sign, that was in fact prepared ahead of time.
The experience then used as proof that the leader is chosen, gifted or specially guided.
Often built on real emotion, real hope and real need, which is why it can feel so convincing from inside.
Sometimes small, like a message that seems to know a member's private details, and sometimes large, like a gathering built around a promised miracle.
what_it_sounds_like: It was no accident that you came today. You were meant to be here.
Did you see what happened when I prayed? That was not me.
The message came to me last night, and it was about you.
Only those who are truly open feel it, and tonight many of you did.
People who left never felt it, which tells you something.
How else could I have known that about your mother?
what_it_is_not: Religious and spiritual experience is real to those who have it, and this entry takes no view on any belief. Ritual, atmosphere and preparation are ordinary in worship. The line is between a prepared setting and an arranged event presented as spontaneous.
A choir, candles, incense or a darkened room used openly to set a mood that everyone knows was planned.
A leader who sincerely believes they received a sign and says so without claiming proof.
A powerful, unplanned moment that moved a congregation, including one nobody can explain.
A magician or stage performer whose audience knows it is a show.
Coincidence. Striking events happen by chance, and noticing one proves nothing about staging.
this_may_be_it_when: Insiders or former helpers say an event they described as spontaneous was planned.
Remarkable events keep happening at just the moments the leader needs support.
Leaders seem to know private details about newcomers without being told.
Members are told that doubting the event means they are spiritually closed.
Questions about how an event happened are met with anger, not a plain explanation.
this_may_not_be_it_when: The event was announced as planned, such as a pageant, reenactment or ceremony.
Members freely say they are unsure what happened and nobody minds.
The leader makes no claim about the experience beyond what people felt.
You only have a secondhand story and have not heard from anyone who was there.
Doubt about the experience is welcomed without being treated as a flaw.
innocent_or_ordinary_possibilities: Warmth, music and shared feeling in a crowd can produce intense experiences with nothing staged.
A leader's insight into people may come from experience reading faces and listening well.
Coincidences get remembered and retold, which can make them seem arranged.
common_false_positives: A well-rehearsed worship service with a dramatic closing song.
A testimony from a member who sincerely felt healed and shares it as personal experience.
A communal ritual with a known script that people join knowingly.
discernment_questions: Was this event presented as planned, or as something that simply happened?
Could someone who was present behind the scenes tell you how it came about, and would they be free to?
Do doubts about it get answers or get treated as a character flaw?
Would you accept the same proof from a stranger making the same claim?
Is the experience used to ask for loyalty, money or obedience afterward?
less_concerning_if: The setting was openly planned and everyone knew it was.
Members can say they felt nothing and still belong.
The experience is offered as meaning, not as proof of anyone's authority.
more_concerning_if: The event is followed by requests for money, devotion or obedience.
People who question how it happened lose standing or are told something is wrong with them.
Participants later report that organizers prepared it in secret.
pattern_over_time_signs: Signs and wonders keep arriving on schedule, always confirming the leader's decisions.
You notice you are waiting for the next sign before making your own choices.
Members who did not have the experience pretend they did.
Earlier events that did not come true are quietly forgotten while the ones that fit are retold.
codex_completed.repair_check: Honest repair would be someone involved saying plainly that an event was arranged, describing what was done, and not asking members to keep treating it as proof. Reframing it as a symbol while keeping the authority it earned is not the same.
codex_completed.boundary_respect_check: Ask how the event came about, and notice whether the reply is an explanation or a verdict on you. A plain answer is respect. Being told your question shows weak faith is the opposite.
codex_completed.psychological_mechanism: A strong experience in a charged setting works as direct evidence for many people, who trust what they felt over what they were told. When it is credited to one person, that person gains a kind of authority argument cannot reach. Admitting it was arranged may seem like losing something real, which makes it harder to revisit.
codex_completed.possible_impact_on_receiver: People describe real awe at the time and later confusion or grief on learning an event was arranged, along with embarrassment at having believed. Some describe being unsure which of their own spiritual experiences were real. Others keep what mattered to them while letting go of the person who claimed credit.

response_options.soft_clarification: Ask a curious, plain question: 'I'd love to understand how that came about. Was it planned in any way?'
response_options.firm_boundary: Decline to treat a single experience as proof: 'I'm glad it moved people. I'm not going to decide anything big based on it.'
response_options.disengagement: Step back from gatherings built around dramatic moments for a while and notice how you feel with some distance.
response_options.support_seeking: Talk with a chaplain, counselor or former member who can discuss spiritual experience without insisting on one answer, and who respects whatever you still believe.
response_options.workplace_or_professional: If a workplace or training program uses staged breakthroughs or 'signs', ask for the curriculum and a participant contact, and speak to an ombuds or HR if the answers are evasive.

codex_completed.boundary_script: "I'm glad that was meaningful to people. I don't want to make any big decisions off one night, so I'm going to take my time."
codex_completed.safety_note: An arranged sign is not a physical danger in itself. The picture changes when the authority it builds is used to demand money or obedience or to cut members off from family, or when members are told that doubting means harm will follow. If that happens, reach someone outside the group, such as a counselor experienced with high-control groups, a legal aid office or a trusted relative.
misuse_warning: Calling someone's sincere spiritual experience staged because you do not share the belief is a dismissal, not a finding. This label is about arrangement kept secret, not about what is true.
Assuming every ritual with theatrical elements is manipulation ignores that most are open about being prepared.
codex_completed.how_to_distinguish_from_related: Sacred Science protects the doctrine from questions, while mystical manipulation produces the experiences that make the leader seem beyond question. Demand for Purity uses shame to hold people in place, where this uses wonder. Milieu Control limits what members can check, which helps staged events stay unexamined. The marker here is an arranged event passed off as spontaneous.

codex_completed.name: Demand for Purity
codex_completed.detectability_note: This tool cannot establish this from pasted text at all. It is included for literacy only, so you can learn to recognize the concept — not as something this tool detects, scores, or flags.
codex_completed.core_meaning: Setting a standard of moral perfection that no one can meet, so members stay ashamed and look only to the group for forgiveness.
codex_completed.short_definition: Setting a standard of moral perfection that no one can meet, so members stay ashamed and look only to the group for forgiveness.
codex_completed.expanded_definition: Demand for purity divides the world into the pure and the corrupt and holds members to a standard of near-perfection in thought, speech and behavior. Because no one can meet it, guilt becomes constant and the group becomes the only source of relief. Confession, public correction and watching one another often go with it. Many traditions hold high standards sincerely. What marks this pattern is a standard drawn so that failure is guaranteed and only the group can absolve it.
codex_completed.plain_language_summary: The rules for being good are set so high that everyone fails, and the only way to feel clean again is to go back to the group.
codex_completed.why_this_matters: A standard nobody can meet keeps a person permanently slightly in the wrong, and the only place to seek relief from that is the authority that set the standard.
what_it_is: A sharp line between pure and impure, with members sorted into one or the other.
Standards covering thoughts, desires and doubts, not only actions.
Rituals of confession or public self-criticism, where lapses are reported to the group.
Shame that is renewed by the rules themselves, since the bar always sits just out of reach.
Relief offered only by the group through its penance, forgiveness or approval.
what_it_sounds_like: A truly devoted person wouldn't have even thought that.
Confess it now, in front of everyone, and you'll feel clean.
Outsiders are contaminated. Being near them pulls you down.
If you still struggle with this, you aren't ready.
We only correct you because we love you.
Everyone here is working on purity. Why aren't you?
what_it_is_not: Many traditions and ethical communities hold demanding standards sincerely, and wanting to be better than you currently are is not shame-based control. What changes the picture is a standard drawn so that falling short is guaranteed and only the group can absolve it.
A faith's fast, vow or discipline that members choose, with a path back after a lapse.
A recovery program that asks for honest accounting and also offers acceptance after setbacks.
A professional code of conduct that holds people accountable for specific behavior.
Personal conscience. Feeling guilty about something you actually did can be healthy.
A strict family or team culture with high expectations that still lets people fail and be forgiven.
this_may_be_it_when: No one can name a member who has ever fully met the standard.
Private thoughts and doubts are treated as moral failures that must be reported.
Forgiveness is granted only by group leaders, never simply by trying again.
People outside are described as unclean, and contact with them is treated as a lapse.
Members feel more shame the longer they stay.
this_may_not_be_it_when: A lapse is met with support and the person returns to standing at once.
Standards cover chosen actions, not private thoughts.
Members can say they are struggling without being punished or ranked.
The community's ideals are described as aspirations that everyone falls short of together.
Confession, if it exists at all, is optional and kept private.
innocent_or_ordinary_possibilities: Ethical traditions often ask for high ideals and honest self-examination, and many people find that meaningful.
New members can feel guilt from their own conscience, not from anyone's pressure.
A leader who is strict about specific safety or conduct rules may simply care about them.
common_false_positives: A religious confession that is voluntary, private and ends with real absolution.
A sports team or military unit with demanding standards of conduct.
A person's own perfectionism, which can exist without any group at all.
discernment_questions: Has anyone you know actually met the standard, and what happened when they did not?
Are your private thoughts treated as something the group has a right to know?
When you fall short, do you feel more shame or more welcome?
Who gets to decide you are forgiven, and can that ever happen without them?
Do you feel clean and light more often now, or heavier?
less_concerning_if: A person who fails is welcomed back without a public process.
Rules concern what people do, and thoughts stay their own.
Members describe the standard as something they chose and can adjust.
more_concerning_if: Confessions are recorded or used later to pressure someone.
Those who admit doubt are shunned, humiliated or made to repeat penance.
Members talk about themselves as worthless or contaminated.
pattern_over_time_signs: The list of things that count as failures gets longer.
You monitor your own thoughts for violations and feel dread when you notice one.
You confess things that once would have seemed too small to mention.
You start to see people outside the group as stained or dangerous.
codex_completed.repair_check: Genuine change would mean the standard itself gets looser: penance ends, confessions stay private, and a lapse leaves a person's standing intact. A leader who apologizes for shaming someone while the same impossible measure stays in place has not changed much.
codex_completed.boundary_respect_check: Try holding back one private thought and see what happens. If the group accepts that some things are yours, that is a good sign. Pressure to hand it over, or a cooler welcome afterward, says otherwise.
codex_completed.psychological_mechanism: Shame tends to push people toward whoever can relieve it. If the rules are set so that failure is certain and only the group can forgive, the group can come to feel like the only safe place. Treating private thoughts as violations can also lead people to police themselves, so that outside control is hardly needed.
codex_completed.possible_impact_on_receiver: People describe constant guilt, scrupulous checking of their own minds, fear of being found out, and a deep sense of being unclean or unworthy. Some describe feeling lighter after stepping away and then grieving the years spent in that state. Others struggle for a long time to trust their own sense of right and wrong.

response_options.soft_clarification: Ask gently about the standard itself: 'Has anyone here ever met this fully? What happens when they don't?'
response_options.firm_boundary: Keep some things private and say so calmly: 'My private thoughts are mine. I'm happy to talk about what I do.'
response_options.disengagement: Sit out a confession or correction session to rest, and spend that time with a person who accepts you as you are.
response_options.support_seeking: Speak with a counselor, therapist or former member who understands shame-based groups, and notice how it feels to be heard without being graded.
response_options.workplace_or_professional: If a program or workplace requires public confessions or ranking people's character, ask for the policy in writing and raise it with an ombuds, HR or legal aid.

codex_completed.boundary_script: "I take my values seriously, and I'm still going to keep my private thoughts to myself. I can talk about what I do, and I'd like that to be enough."
codex_completed.safety_note: Watch for confessions being used as pressure, shame that turns into thoughts of self-harm, penances that involve deprivation or pain, or fear of what happens to those who are found impure. If you feel unsafe with yourself, reach a crisis line or emergency services right away. Plans for stepping away are best made privately, with a counselor or advocate who knows high-control groups.
misuse_warning: Calling a faith or ethical community shame-based because its standards are high ignores that many people choose such standards freely. The test is whether failure is guaranteed and only the group can absolve it.
Telling someone their guilt is entirely manufactured can dismiss real conscience about real harm they did.
codex_completed.how_to_distinguish_from_related: Sacred Science makes the doctrine unquestionable; demand for purity makes you unworthy by its measure. Doctrine Over Person says your experience is wrong, while this says your self is stained. Dispensing of Existence ranks people by worth and treats outsiders as lesser, whereas this keeps insiders permanently short of the standard.
codex_completed.detection_notes: Not matched or scored. Pasted personal text cannot establish an institutional- or societal-scale pattern — that requires independent, corroborated, documented evidence at a completely different scale.

codex_completed.name: Sacred Science
codex_completed.detectability_note: This tool cannot establish this from pasted text at all. It is included for literacy only, so you can learn to recognize the concept — not as something this tool detects, scores, or flags.
codex_completed.core_meaning: Treating the group's doctrine as beyond question, so that doubts are read as a flaw in the doubter instead of a reason to examine the claim.
codex_completed.short_definition: Treating the group's doctrine as beyond question, so that doubts are read as a flaw in the doubter instead of a reason to examine the claim.
codex_completed.expanded_definition: Sacred science is when a group's founding ideas are placed above evidence, argument and revision, and questioning them is treated as disloyalty or weakness. The ideas may be religious, political, therapeutic or even scientific in tone. What marks it is not how strongly people believe, but that the claims cannot be tested, and the questioner's character becomes the subject. Every field has assumptions it does not reopen daily; the difference is whether questions are allowed to matter.
codex_completed.plain_language_summary: The group's central ideas can't be questioned. If you doubt them, the problem is said to be you, not the ideas.
codex_completed.why_this_matters: Doubt gets recoded as a fault in the doubter rather than a question about the claim, so the ordinary means of testing an idea are unavailable from inside.
what_it_is: A set of core claims declared final, complete or beyond ordinary checking.
Doubt interpreted as pride, weakness, ignorance, or lack of commitment.
Outside evidence that contradicts the claims dismissed in advance as the work of enemies.
A technical or scientific vocabulary that sounds precise but cannot be tested or revised.
Found in some religious, political, therapeutic and self-help movements, though most are open to challenge.
what_it_sounds_like: The teaching is not something you evaluate. You live it.
Your questions show you aren't ready for the next level.
Real students don't need proof.
Critics don't understand because they haven't done the work.
Doubting the method means doubting yourself.
The science here is settled, and we don't revisit it.
what_it_is_not: Strong conviction is not this, and every field has foundational assumptions it does not reopen daily. The flag is a body of ideas that cannot be questioned without the questioner's character or loyalty becoming the subject instead.
A scientific or religious consensus that still welcomes challenge and revision through evidence or argument.
A teacher who asks students to try a practice for a season before judging it, while saying critics are welcome.
A committed believer who disagrees with critics, even strongly, and still lets others differ.
Faith, which many people hold sincerely and which need not claim to be evidence.
An expert declining to debate a question that has been well settled.
this_may_be_it_when: Asking how a claim is known draws comments about your attitude.
No finding, whatever it showed, would be accepted as a reason to change the teaching.
People who left or criticized are explained away by their flaws before anyone reads what they said.
Evidence from outside is declared irrelevant because only insiders can understand.
Members learn to keep their questions to themselves.
this_may_not_be_it_when: Members debate the teaching openly and sometimes change it.
Leaders have admitted past errors and corrected them in public.
Critics' arguments are read and answered on their merits.
You are only being asked to practice something before judging it.
People disagree inside the group and nobody loses standing for it.
innocent_or_ordinary_possibilities: A new member may simply not yet know the reasoning behind a teaching.
A seasoned teacher may be tired of repeating answers that have been given many times.
Some traditions treat core texts as sacred while welcoming questions about interpretation.
common_false_positives: A physics teacher who won't debate settled results with a student who has not studied them.
A congregation that treats its scripture as sacred and also welcomes honest questions.
A discipline that asks beginners to follow the method before they critique it.
discernment_questions: What evidence, if it appeared, would the group accept as a reason to change this teaching?
When someone raises a doubt, is the doubt answered or is the person assessed?
Have the central claims ever been revised, and can anyone say what changed?
Are you free to read the strongest criticism and then decide?
Do people who disagree stay in good standing?
less_concerning_if: Questions are met with reasons, including 'we don't know yet'.
Disagreement within the group happens openly and is not punished.
The group's claims are described as one view among others.
more_concerning_if: Asking questions leads to loss of standing, relationships or work.
Contradicting evidence is turned into proof of persecution.
The doctrine is used to justify harm to those who question it.
pattern_over_time_signs: You stop asking questions aloud, then stop asking them yourself.
You find yourself defending ideas you could not explain from first principles.
You begin to see critics as simply unable to understand.
Each time doubts arise you blame yourself, not the claim.
codex_completed.repair_check: Meaningful change would mean questions get real answers, past errors get named, and a dissenter keeps their standing. A speech praising open inquiry, while questioners still fall out of favor, fixes only the speech.
codex_completed.boundary_respect_check: Put one question to the group and watch what it costs. If the answer engages the question, the claim is open to checking. If the response is about your loyalty, motives or readiness, the claim is being shielded.
codex_completed.psychological_mechanism: When doubt is treated as a personal failing, a person may hide it, and a hidden doubt can seem like proof of being the only one who has it. Hearing that the teaching is complete also makes it look safer than examining it. The habit of testing claims can weaken from disuse.
codex_completed.possible_impact_on_receiver: People describe silencing their own questions, fear of what doubt says about them, and difficulty weighing evidence after leaving. Some describe anger at having been told questions meant weakness, and relief at discovering ordinary inquiry is allowed. Others describe a long stretch of not trusting any source of authority.

response_options.soft_clarification: Ask a sincere question aloud: 'What would we expect to see if this teaching were wrong?'
response_options.firm_boundary: Keep thinking for yourself and say so plainly: 'I'm going to look at how this holds up before I decide.'
response_options.disengagement: Take a break from study sessions and use the time to read widely, including sources the group dislikes.
response_options.support_seeking: Talk with someone outside who has no stake, such as a teacher, counselor or former member, and test your questions on them.
response_options.workplace_or_professional: If a company or program treats its method as beyond question, ask for the evidence in writing and keep a record of how the questions were answered.

codex_completed.boundary_script: "I believe in testing things, and I'm going to keep doing that with this too. If the teaching is sound, it should survive a few questions."
codex_completed.safety_note: An unquestionable doctrine is not a physical danger by itself. It raises concern when questioning brings threats, shunning, loss of housing or income, or when the doctrine is used to deny medical care or to justify harm. If that happens, speak to a counselor who knows high-control groups, a legal aid office or a trusted relative before acting.
misuse_warning: Calling any strong belief sacred science dismisses people for being sure of themselves. The test is whether questions can be asked and answered, not whether conviction runs deep.
Using the label to mock someone's faith turns a description of a closed system into an insult.
codex_completed.how_to_distinguish_from_related: Doctrine Over Person tells you that your own experience is wrong when it clashes with the teaching, while sacred science declares the teaching itself closed to testing. Milieu Control limits what reaches you, whereas this governs how you treat what does. Mystical Manipulation produces experiences that seem to prove the leader; here the claim simply cannot be challenged.
codex_completed.detection_notes: Not matched or scored. Pasted personal text cannot establish an institutional- or societal-scale pattern — that requires independent, corroborated, documented evidence at a completely different scale.

codex_completed.name: Doctrine Over Person
codex_completed.detectability_note: This tool cannot establish this from pasted text at all. It is included for literacy only, so you can learn to recognize the concept — not as something this tool detects, scores, or flags.
codex_completed.core_meaning: Teaching members that when their own experience, memory or conscience contradicts the group's doctrine, the experience is what must be wrong.
codex_completed.short_definition: Teaching members that when their own experience, memory or conscience contradicts the group's doctrine, the experience is what must be wrong.
codex_completed.expanded_definition: Doctrine over person means a member's lived experience is never allowed to count against the group's teaching. If something harmed them, or a memory disagrees with the official story, they are told they misunderstood, were not yet ready, or sinned by doubting. Committed groups often ask for belief that cuts against immediate feeling, such as forgiveness or discipline. The distinguishing question is whether a contradicting experience can ever count as evidence, or is always rewritten as the member's own failure.
codex_completed.plain_language_summary: When what you lived through does not match what the group teaches, you are told you are the one who is mistaken.
codex_completed.why_this_matters: When lived experience is always the thing that must be wrong, a person loses the only instrument they have for noticing that something is harming them.
what_it_is: A member's account of harm, pain or confusion answered by pointing back to the teaching.
Memories that differ from the group's official history declared false or distorted.
Conscience treated as a symptom of weakness when it conflicts with what leaders say.
Present in groups of many kinds, from religious to political to commercial, though most let personal experience count.
Often gentle in tone, delivered as concern for the member's growth.
what_it_sounds_like: That's not what happened. That's how your ego remembers it.
If the teaching says it's good for you, then the pain is part of the problem.
You felt hurt because you're still attached to your old self.
The leaders couldn't have done that. You must have misunderstood.
Your gut feeling is just fear talking.
Trust the teaching over your own mind.
what_it_is_not: Committed communities routinely ask members to hold a belief that cuts against immediate feeling, such as fasting or forgiveness, and that alone is not this. The question is whether a contradicting experience can count as evidence, or is always reclassified as the member's failure.
A therapist or mentor who gently challenges a distorted self-view while taking the person's experience seriously.
Two people honestly remembering an event differently and being willing to check.
A teacher who says a feeling may pass and still listens when it does not.
Self-doubt that comes from a person's own anxiety, with no group pressing it.
A friend disagreeing with how you read someone's motives.
this_may_be_it_when: Every report of harm is turned into a lesson about the person reporting it.
Members who remember events differently from the official story are told they are wrong.
A conscience objection is treated as pride, doubt or lack of faith.
The same response comes back no matter what the experience was.
You have stopped trusting your own reactions and check them against the teaching first.
this_may_not_be_it_when: Members' accounts lead to changes in the group's practice.
A leader says, 'I may have been wrong, tell me more'.
Disagreement is welcome and the person's experience is taken seriously.
The teaching is offered as guidance and members can say it did not work for them.
Concerns about misconduct go to someone independent.
innocent_or_ordinary_possibilities: A person may sincerely be misreading a situation, and a gentle correction can help.
Traditions of discipline may ask people to set aside a passing feeling for a larger aim.
Memory is fallible, and two honest people can disagree about what happened.
common_false_positives: A coach who tells an athlete to push through discomfort while watching for real injury.
A faith community counseling forgiveness after a wrong while also supporting accountability.
A family disagreement about what was said at a holiday dinner.
discernment_questions: When your experience conflicts with the teaching, which one is expected to give way?
Has a member's report of harm ever changed anything the group does?
Do you check your feelings against the teaching before you trust them?
Can you name something you saw or felt that was acknowledged as real even though it contradicted the doctrine?
Are concerns about leaders heard by anyone outside the leadership?
less_concerning_if: Members' concerns are acknowledged first, and teaching follows second.
Leaders can say they got something wrong and point to what changed.
Different recollections are treated as something to sort out together.
more_concerning_if: Reports of abuse or harm are turned back on the person who reported them.
Members are told to ignore physical symptoms, grief or fear because the teaching says otherwise.
Those who trust their own memory are labeled unstable or rebellious.
pattern_over_time_signs: You hesitate to name a feeling until you've checked whether it fits.
Painful experiences are filed away as personal failings instead of discussed.
You apologize for reactions you used to think were reasonable.
Old friends mention you used to trust your own judgment more.
codex_completed.repair_check: Honest repair would be a leader saying the experience was real and the teaching was part of the problem, then changing something concrete. Praise for the member's growth, with no change to how accounts of harm are handled, repairs nothing.
codex_completed.boundary_respect_check: Describe something that happened exactly as you saw it, then watch whether the reply begins with your account or with the doctrine. Starting with what you said is respect. Starting with what you ought to have felt is not.
codex_completed.psychological_mechanism: Many people are inclined to trust a group's account over their own, especially when the group offers belonging and meaning. If every contradicting experience is explained as a personal failing, a member may learn to distrust their reactions, and the habit can carry into areas the group never addressed.
codex_completed.possible_impact_on_receiver: People describe not trusting their own memory or feelings, silence about harm they experienced, and difficulty making decisions without checking with someone first. After leaving, some describe slowly relearning how to listen to themselves. Many describe a mix of anger and grief at the years their own experience was set aside.

response_options.soft_clarification: State what you saw and ask if it can count: 'This is what happened for me. Can we treat that as real and talk about it?'
response_options.firm_boundary: Hold your own account without arguing it: 'That is my experience, and I'm not going to call it wrong.'
response_options.disengagement: Pause a conversation that is turning into a verdict on you and write your account down privately for yourself.
response_options.support_seeking: Share what happened with someone who knew you before the group and ask how it sounds to them, or with a counselor who understands high-control groups.
response_options.workplace_or_professional: If a program or workplace treats complaints as personal flaws, put your account in writing with dates and take it to HR, an ombuds or an outside regulator.

codex_completed.boundary_script: "I know what I experienced, and it matters to me. I'd like us to start from that, even if it does not fit the teaching."
codex_completed.safety_note: Being told your experience is wrong is not by itself a physical danger. It becomes serious when the pattern is used to hide abuse or to deny medical care, or when reporting harm brings retaliation. In that case put your account in writing, reach an outside advocate, a doctor, legal aid or a trusted person, and call emergency services if you are in danger.
misuse_warning: Calling every disagreement with your experience this pattern can shut down honest correction. It fits when experience is never allowed to count, not when it is questioned once.
Using the label against a friend who offers a different view of an event can turn a conversation into a verdict.
codex_completed.how_to_distinguish_from_related: Sacred Science protects the doctrine from outside testing, whereas doctrine over person is what happens to your own memory and feelings when they clash with it. Milieu Control restricts what you can see and who you can speak to, but not what you conclude. Bounded Choice shapes which options feel real; this one discounts what you have already lived.
codex_completed.detection_notes: Not matched or scored. Pasted personal text cannot establish an institutional- or societal-scale pattern — that requires independent, corroborated, documented evidence at a completely different scale.

codex_completed.name: Dispensing of Existence
codex_completed.detectability_note: This tool cannot establish this from pasted text at all. It is included for literacy only, so you can learn to recognize the concept — not as something this tool detects, scores, or flags.
codex_completed.core_meaning: A group's doctrine ranks people by whether they deserve to exist or count as fully human, so that harm to outsiders, critics and former members is treated as justified.
codex_completed.short_definition: A group's doctrine ranks people by whether they deserve to exist or count as fully human, so that harm to outsiders, critics and former members is treated as justified.
codex_completed.expanded_definition: Dispensing of Existence is one of Robert Lifton's eight themes of thought reform: the group decides whose life has worth. People outside it, and those who leave or object, are described as lost, evil, contaminated or less than human. Strong boundaries alone do not make this pattern, since many communities have membership rules. What marks it is that worth itself is withdrawn, so cruelty toward outsiders feels like virtue and members learn their own standing could be withdrawn the same way.
codex_completed.plain_language_summary: The group teaches that people who disagree or walk away are worth less, or are not really people at all, so treating them badly starts to feel right instead of wrong.
codex_completed.why_this_matters: When worth is handed out by doctrine, people outside the group can be shunned, mocked or harmed without anyone feeling they did wrong. Members also learn that their own standing is conditional, which makes doubt feel dangerous and staying feel like the only safe place.
what_it_is: A sorting of humanity into those who count and those who do not, done by doctrine rather than by anything a person actually did.
Language for outsiders and leavers that strips away personhood: lost, dead to us, vermin, beyond saving.
Treating critics and former members as if they had stopped existing, with their names unspoken and their messages unanswered.
A moral frame in which harshness toward the unworthy is praised, so the people carrying it out feel pride instead of guilt.
A rule that turns inward too: a member judged unworthy can be declared worthless by the same logic.
what_it_sounds_like: He's not our brother anymore. He chose death when he walked out.
Those people out there are just the walking dead.
She doesn't exist to us now. Don't say her name.
Anyone who questions this teaching has already shown they have no soul.
The world's people can't be hurt the way we can. They aren't fully awake.
Pray for the lost, but don't expect them to feel anything.
what_it_is_not: Strong boundaries such as membership rules, excommunication or shunning are not automatically this; many communities have exit rules while still treating leavers as full people.
A group that says its beliefs are true and others are mistaken. Claiming to be right is not the same as saying others have no worth.
Sharp anger at one person for something they did, which is about conduct and can end, not about whether they count as human.
Religious teaching that every person is valued, where a leaver is missed and still welcome to visit, write or call.
Ordinary in-group loyalty, such as a sports rivalry or national pride, where the other side is mocked but nobody doubts they are people.
this_may_be_it_when: Former members or critics are spoken of as dead, empty, evil or subhuman, not merely as mistaken.
Mistreating an outsider is described as service to the cause or to the divine.
Members are expected to feel nothing, or satisfaction, when something bad happens to a critic.
Contact with a leaver is treated as contamination, even for their own parents or children.
A member who falls out of favor is suddenly discussed in the same terms as outsiders.
this_may_not_be_it_when: People who go can still visit, write and be welcomed as the relatives and friends they are.
Outsiders are described as wrong or misguided but also as people with goodness, families and worth.
A rule such as not dating outside the group is stated openly and is not paired with contempt for those outside.
Members can voice sympathy for a critic without being punished.
The harsh words were said once in anger and later withdrawn.
innocent_or_ordinary_possibilities: A community grieving a departure may say painful things like 'we lost him' that express sadness, not a verdict on his worth.
Crude jokes or slang among members about outsiders can exist without shaping how anyone is actually treated.
Old religious language about being 'lost' or 'dead in sin' is, in many traditions, paired with a duty to love the person so described.
common_false_positives: A congregation that limits contact for a stated offense, explains how to return, and still treats the person as a person.
A political or sports rivalry in which each side calls the other terrible names but nobody is denied basic respect.
A family estrangement where relatives stopped speaking to someone after real harm.
discernment_questions: When someone leaves this group or criticizes it, are they still spoken of as a person with a name and a story?
Is anyone allowed to say kind things about a former member, or to stay in touch, without being punished?
Does the doctrine give reasons hurting an outsider would be wrong, or only reasons it would be fine?
If I were declared unworthy tomorrow, what would the group do, and who would stay beside me?
Would I treat a stranger the way critics are treated here if nobody had told me they were lesser?
less_concerning_if: Outsiders and leavers are still greeted, helped in an emergency and remembered by name.
Disagreement with the teaching is sometimes discussed openly, and no one is declared worthless for it.
The group's own writings or leaders state plainly that every person has worth.
more_concerning_if: Violence, harassment, or the taking of belongings or children is aimed at people the group has ranked lower.
Members are told that harm to a leaver is deserved or even required.
The ranking is used to justify keeping someone from medical care, housing or contact with family.
pattern_over_time_signs: The words for outsiders harden from 'mistaken' to 'lost' to 'dead' to 'not human'.
More people are added to the unworthy list, including members who asked questions.
Members stop mentioning outside friends or relatives because those people have been sorted into the unworthy group.
Your own sympathy for someone outside begins to feel like a betrayal you have to hide.
codex_completed.repair_check: A changed practice is the test: leavers named again, contact allowed, harsh language about them withdrawn, members free to speak kindly of them. A regretful sermon that leaves the shunning list and the vocabulary untouched changes nothing.
codex_completed.boundary_respect_check: What happens to the member who mentions a leaver kindly? If they are heard, even with disagreement, the group still treats that leaver as a person. If they are corrected, watched or put on a list themselves, the ranking is still doing its work.
codex_completed.psychological_mechanism: Seeing a group of people as lesser can lower the usual discomfort of hurting them. When that view arrives through a respected doctrine, it can pass for moral clarity instead of prejudice.
